label: S0059
statement:
T11-D: REFUTATION of an unverified padded-permanent multiplicity table (gpt-oss-120b, NOT_VERIFIED) AND a course-correction on obstruction-hunting. (a) The model claimed a_{(5,1)}=1 for the padded perm_2 at (m,n,d)=(2,3,2). CONTAINMENT ARGUMENT: dc(perm_2)=2 <= 3, so the padded perm_2 = l^1 perm_2 lies IN the orbit closure of det_3 (Z_{2,3} subset D_3); restriction C[D_3] ->> C[Z_{2,3}] is surjective, giving a_lambda <= delta_lambda <= g(lambda,(d^n),(d^n)) for ALL lambda. My VERIFIED g((5,1),(2,2,2),(2,2,2))=0 (T11-C) therefore forces a_{(5,1)}=0, contradicting the table. Table rejected. (b) COURSE-CORRECTION: the case (m,n)=(2,3) is DEGENERATE for obstruction-hunting - since perm_2 is contained in closure(det_3), NO separation exists, so NO occurrence OR multiplicity obstruction can exist there by definition. A candidate requires (m,n) with perm_m NOT in closure(det_n), i.e. n < dc(perm_m). Since dc(perm_3)=7 (Alper-Bogart-Velasco; Mignon-Ressayre lower bound m^2/2), the smallest NON-DEGENERATE padded case is m=3, n in {4,5,6}. Any obstruction search must use this regime, not (2,3).

label: S0069
statement:
REJECTED: the proposed extension of the null-cone lemma to NON-rectangular partitions, and the claimed d_min^sep(3,4) >= 9. MATH ERROR: for a non-rectangular lambda with ell=k, the HWV transforms as P_lambda(g(t).f) = t^w P_lambda(f) with w = k*lambda_1 - |lambda| != 0. Then lim_{t->0} t^w P_lambda(f) = 0 for w>0 holds for ANY value of P_lambda(f), giving NO information - one CANNOT conclude P_lambda(f)=0. The null-cone argument works ONLY for w=0 (rectangular lambda=(d^k) = SL_k-invariant), where P_lambda(g(t).f)=P_lambda(f) is constant so P_lambda(f)=P_lambda(0)=0. ADVERSARIAL CONFIRMATION (exact computation): lambda=(12,2,2,2,2) has w=5*12-20=40>0; the flawed lemma predicts vanishing on Y, but the HWV evaluates NONZERO on z*perm_3 (e.g. 103363705/13824, 1785096875/27 at random 5-planes) => delta_perm=1, consistent with my original d=5 report (22 of 23 five-row HWVs non-vanishing on perm). Direct contradiction => extension invalid. CORRECTED STATUS: only d_min^sep(3,4) >= 6 stands (from rectangular T11-N + BHIM symmetroid bound for ell<=4 up to degree 8 + the 23 five-row d=5 certificates). d_min^sep(3,4) >= 9 is NOT proven. LMR PRECISIONS (owner): LMR Thm 3.1.1 gives degree-2n(n-1) equations but does NOT prove this is the MINIMAL separation degree; LMR equations are not automatically certified separators without checking non-vanishing on Y; the Hessian criterion concerns rank at points of the hypersurface {f=0}, not the whole space (Hess(det_n) at the identity is non-degenerate). So 'degree 24 = proven minimum' is unjustified. VALID OPEN TASK: for d=6,7,8 and non-rectangular ell>=5 partitions, determine structurally whether ker E_D not subset ker E_Y can occur; no valid null-cone shortcut exists for the non-rectangular case.

label: S0083
statement:
Slice route: level-m slices of f_n are coNP-hard (padding); monotone and general circuit size are polynomially related on slices (Berkowitz), so a superpolynomial monotone bound for them would prove P != NP (equivalent reformulation). Span-program analogue: mSP and SP polynomially related on slices, loss SP >= (mSP - 2N)/(N-1): all PNP-001 bounds (<= N+1) vanish under transfer. Generic Gal constructions on slices are natural-proofs-blocked (assuming NC^1 PRFs); a method must use function-specific structure.
PREMISES: Berkowitz 1982 (cited)

statement:

GF(p)-blind MUS in the D-018 sense are defined only for k = p.

label: S0107
statement:
D4 REUSE-TO-CORRELATION DECOMPOSITION (exact): let C be a De Morgan circuit with gamma gates g_1..g_gamma of fan-out > 1 and S gates. For a in {0,1}^gamma let F_a(x) = AND_j [P_j(x,a) = a_j] AND P_out(x,a), where P_j, P_out are the principal formulas (CHOPRS20 Thm 30) with reused gates replaced by constants a. Then L(F_a) <= S+gamma, the F_a have pairwise disjoint supports and C = OR_a F_a. For any two distributions Y, Z: Pr_Y[C]-Pr_Z[C] = sum_a (Pr_Y[F_a]-Pr_Z[F_a]), so some formula F_a of size <= S+gamma has advantage >= Adv(C)/2^gamma. Reuse costs a factor 2^gamma in CORRELATION, not in size (T07 pays it in size).

label: S0109
statement:
D5 QUANTIFIER CHECK against OPS21: required is ONE fixed eps>0 that works for ALL sufficiently small beta>0, against general circuits. D2 meets the quantifier form (any fixed eps<1/2 for every beta) but only for De Morgan circuits with r <= (1+beta-2eps)log2 N reused gates. label: S0110
statement:
D6 REUSE COLLAPSE UNDER RESTRICTION (repair of the D5 limit): let d_g be the number of input variables gate g depends on. Under a truly random p-restriction, a reused gate stays a non-literal, non-constant reused gate only if >= 2 of its d_g variables stay live, so Pr <= C(d_g,2) p^2 <= p^2 d_g^2/2 (union over pairs) and E[gamma(C|rho)] <= sum_{g reused} min(1, p^2 d_g^2/2). With p = N^{beta+eps/5-1}: reused gates with d_g <= N^{1-beta-eta} contribute <= N^{-2 eta}, so only WIDE reused gates (d_g > N^{1-beta-eta}) can survive. Combined with AF: if P1, P2 hold, Gap-MCSP[N^beta] has no De Morgan circuit of size N^{1+eps} with at most N^{beta-2eta} wide reused gates (Markov over rho). Sanity check (dual-rail parity): the tree has ~N/2^j reused nodes with d_g = 2^j; sum_j (N/2^j) min(1,p^2 4^j) = Theta(pN) = Theta(k) survivors, matching counterexample 1 - those survivors are exactly the wide nodes (d_g >= 1/p). REMAINING OBLIGATION (unrestricted circuits): circuits computing Gap-MCSP[N^beta] with more than N^beta wide reused gates.
PREMISES: D4; AF; D5

label: S0124
statement:
ST2 INDEPENDENT TRANSFER, STRENGTHENED (author Claude family; owner's sec. 9 argument with P = NP replaced by NP subset P/poly): let S be polylog-uniform AC0_d[2^{m^k}] with r CX rounds, uniformity time m^u. Bit i of X_j is a Sigma_{d'}-TIME[poly(m, L_j, log b)] predicate g_j(i, b, D_<j) with random access to the earlier answers D_<j (padding zeros beyond the description). Assume NP subset P/poly, so PH subset P/poly and Sigma_{d'} has circuits of size n^{c}. Induction: if every earlier answer has size <= m^{K_i}, hardwiring b and D_<j gives a circuit for X_j of size m^{K_j}, K_j = c*O(K_{j-1} + k + u), independent of b. Hence: absolute protocol => NP notsubset P/poly (stronger than Thm 1.7's P != NP). Uses neither Lemma 5.4 nor SearchMCSP.

label: S0134
statement:
W-D FIRST FAILING INFERENCE: (i) a polylogtime-uniform AC0 refuter has (log n)^{O(1)} alternating time per output bit, A has (log n)^{f(n)} state bits, f = omega(1): the refuter cannot simulate A, so it cannot search for a colliding pair. (ii) refuter outputs have circuit complexity <= c(log n)^c (CJSW Lemma 2.5): 2^{O((log n)^c log log n)} such prefixes versus 2^{(log n)^{f(n)}} states, so for f > c+1 counting forces NO collision among refuter-describable prefixes. Hence the uniform-collision obligation is exactly: no admissible A is injective on simple prefixes with (log n)^f-time updates - the update-cost (O*) obligation for DISJ (CJ4). Repair direction: non-injectivity from transition cost (route M update-map results S0036/S0037), not from counting.

label: S0135
statement:
QO1 UPPER BOUND UNDER NP in P/poly (derivation of the OPS21 Thm 1.4 mechanism, author Claude family): NP subset SIZE[n^a] => there is K=K(a) such that for EVERY s=s(n) with n <= s <= 2^{n/2}: Gap-MCSP[s/(cn), s] on N=2^n bits has circuits of size N*s^K (a.e.). Proof: s'=s/(cn). Greedy anti-checker: V_0 = all circuits of size <= s', Y_0 = empty. Step i: for every position y in [N] (a fixed wire x_y) evaluate an approximate count of |{C in V_i: C(y) != x_y}|/|V_i| given (Y_i, x|Y_i, y, x_y) - input length L = O(t n), Stockmeyer approximate counting is in BPP^NP subset Sigma_3 subset P/poly (Karp-Lipton chain) so size L^{a'}; a tournament over the N candidates picks the best (y, x_y): N*L^{a'} gates per step. Elimination: if CC(x) > s then for every nonempty V_i some y kills >= 1/3 of V_i (minimax on V_i: otherwise a distribution over V_i is correct w.p. > 2/3 on every input and the majority of O(n) samples computes x with size O(n s') <= s, contradiction); with approximation >= 1/4. Hence V_t = empty after t = O(s' log s') steps. YES (CC(x) <= s'): the circuit for x is never eliminated. Final test 'V_t empty' is coNP on L bits. Total t*N*L^{a'} = N*s^{K}, K = a'+2, independent of s and beta. With s = N^beta: g_beta(N) <= N^{1+K beta} for all beta in (0,1/2]. c is the constant from the majority step (not necessarily 10).
PREMISES: OPS21 Thm 1.4 / Lemma 4.1 (anti-checker); CHOPRS20 Lemma 27; Stockmeyer approximate counting; Karp-Lipton: NP in P/poly => PH in P/poly
PROOF:

label: S0136
statement:
QO2 WEAKEST SUFFICIENT QUANTIFIER FORM Q*: if for every K >= 1 there is a size function s_K (n <= s_K <= 2^{n/2}) such that Gap-MCSP[s_K/(cn), s_K] has no circuits of size N*s_K^K for infinitely many n, then NP notsubset P/poly, hence P != NP (contrapositive of QO1). Special cases: Q1 (exists eps, all small beta: g_beta notin O(N^{1+eps})) => Q2 (for all k, delta exists beta < delta: g_beta notin O(N^{1+k beta}); take beta < min(delta, eps/k)) => Q* (s_K = N^beta). Q3 (fixed s = n^c, g notin O(N log^k N) for all k) => Q*. Lower bounds whose exponent ratio eps(beta)/beta is bounded (eps = beta, 2 beta) do NOT suffice since K is unknown; eps = sqrt(beta), beta log(1/beta) or N*(log N)^{omega(1)} at s = polylog do. LOCALITY (CHOPRS20): the QO1 circuits are N*poly(s) wires into fan-in-poly(s) PH predicates, so any proof of Q* must fail against such oracle circuits.
PREMISES: QO1

statement:

label: S0144
statement:
statement_start: LEMMA (Corrected Reuse Collapse under Random Restriction): Let C be a De Morgan circuit of size |C| <= N^{1+eps} with a set of reused gates G_reused. For each g in G_reused let d_g be the number of input variables g depends on. Let p = N^{beta + eps/5 - 1} with beta > 0, eps >= 0. Under a random p-restriction rho, a reused gate g stays a non-literal, non-constant reused gate iff at least 2 of its d_g variables remain live. For any threshold D* = N^{(1-beta)/2 - eta - 7eps/10} with eta > 0, define W(C) = sum_{g in G_reused} min(1, p^2 d_g^2 / 2). Then E[gamma(C|rho)] <= W(C), where gamma(C|rho) is the number of surviving non-literal reused gates. If every reused gate has d_g <= D*, then W(C) <= (1/2) N^{beta - 2eta}. Consequently Pr[gamma(C|rho) > N^{beta - eta}] <= (1/2) N^{-eta} by Markov's inequality.
statement_end: Consequently Pr[gamma(C|rho) > N^{beta - eta}] <= (1/2) N^{-eta} by Markov's inequality.

structure.evidence: REPAIR of refuted D6 (S0110, S0113) and algebraically-flawed D6' (S0142). The threshold D* = N^{(1-beta)/2 - eta - 7eps/10} is derived by solving W(C) <= N^{beta-2eta}/2 for the exponent alpha where d_g <= N^alpha. With p = N^{beta+eps/5-1}, p^2 = N^{2beta+2eps/5-2}. For d_g <= D* = N^alpha, contribution per gate <= (1/2) N^{2alpha} N^{2beta+2eps/5-2}. With <= N^{1+eps} gates, total W(C) <= (1/2) N^{1+eps+2alpha+2beta+2eps/5-2} = (1/2) N^{2alpha+2beta+7eps/5-1}. Setting 2alpha+2beta+7eps/5-1 <= beta-2eta gives alpha <= (1-beta)/2 - 7eps/10 - eta. This D* is larger (weaker threshold) than the original D6's N^{1-beta-eta} because (1-beta)/2 < 1-beta for beta in (0,1). The residual class R' = {C: W(C) > N^{beta-2eta}} is therefore larger than the original R, making the surviving obligation harder but the lemma correct. No dependency on P1/P2; this is a pure counting bound.

label: S0145
statement:
EXCLUSION E-LEVIN (mechanism, not the statement): (a) for Levin's universal search U and every fixed algorithm A that outputs SAT witnesses, t_U(F) <= 2^{|A|} (t_A(F) + v(|F|)) with v the witness check time; hence 'U runs in polynomial time on all satisfiable F' <=> P = NP, and a lower bound for U is up to a constant factor a lower bound for every algorithm - the quantifier over algorithms is not removed. (b) Relative to an oracle A with P^A = NP^A (BGS, seq 3), U^A runs in polynomial time; every argument that uses U only through simulation and diagonalization relativizes and cannot show U superpolynomial. Excluded: pure simulation/diagonalization against U. Not excluded: arguments that use the Cook-Levin encoding of U's run non-black-box (short encodings of long computations); the only mechanism known to work there is the algorithmic method of Williams (succinct SAT), whose proven reach is NEXP/NQP lower bounds against ACC-type classes, not P != NP.

label: S0147
statement:

label: S0151
statement:
QUANTIFIER Q-WILLIAMS (owner 2026-11-26): 'for every k there is L_k in NP with L_k not in SIZE(n^k)' does not imply P != NP: by Kannan 1982, Sigma2 cap Pi2 is not in SIZE(n^k) for every fixed k; under P = NP, PH = P, so already P contains such an L_k for every k. Needed is the uniform-quantifier form 'EXISTS L in NP FORALL k: L not in SIZE(n^k)' (NP not in P/poly), or the uniform analogue for DTIME. Fixed-polynomial NP lower bounds and NQP lower bounds (Murray-Williams) are not approximations of P != NP.

label: S0153
statement:
T-NORM-F (refines seq 17140; CONDITIONAL on D4 seq 16760 and CORR-IK): the forest-size estimate s = p^2 N^{1+eps} is wrong in general. Tal's shrinkage E[L(F|rho)] = O(p^2 L log(1/p) + p sqrt(L)) applies per principal formula; with m principal formulas of sizes L_i (sum L_i = L <= N^{1+eps}, m up to N^{1+eps}), E[s] <= sum_i min(p L_i, O~(p^2 L_i + p sqrt(L_i))) <= O~(p^2 L + p sqrt(m L)), and circuits with all L_i = O(1) reach s ~ p L = N^{beta+6eps/5}. Worst case k^2/s >= p^2 N^2 / (2 p N^{1+eps}) = N^{beta-4eps/5}/2 (k = pN = N^{beta+eps/5}). Against D4's correlation >= 2^{-N^{beta-eta}} (w.p. >= 1 - N^{-eta} - 0.1 for gamma and s, Markov) the contradiction holds iff eta > 4eps/5 (+o(1)); with W budget N^{beta-2eta} >= 1 this needs 4eps/5 < eta < beta/2, i.e. eps < 5beta/8. The owner's conditions 1 - eps > beta - eta and beta + 6eps/5 < 1 used the formula-only size and are insufficient for general circuits.

label: S0155
statement:
SEED-FLOOR (proof of the D5 claim, seq 16768): if a distribution G on {0,1}^k has support size <= M (e.g. seed length l, M = 2^l), then some AND of t = floor(log2 M) + 1 <= k literals has |Pr_G - Pr_U| >= 2^{-t}: of the 2^t patterns on the first t coordinates at most M < 2^t are hit, a missed pattern has Pr_G = 0 and Pr_U = 2^{-t}. Hence fooling De Morgan formulas of size >= t with error delta forces log2 M >= log2(1/delta) - 1. In the D4/AF mechanism (error 2^{-r-2} for r surviving reused gates): seed >= r + 1, and since YES outputs G(z) o rho have circuit size <= N^beta, the support on the star coordinates is <= 2^{O(N^beta log N)}, so r <= O(N^beta log N). Consequence: every PRG instantiation of AF has polylog(1/delta)-exponent a >= 1 and covers at most N^{beta+o(1)} surviving reused gates; circuits with more surviving reuse must first be reduced by D6'/NORM.

statement:

label: S0158
statement:
D4-SIM (owner check 2026-11-26: restriction chosen before or after the assignment a?): no selection effect. Every F_a = AND_j [P_j(x,a) = a_j] AND P_out(x,a) is a constant substitution in ONE forest Phi of principal formulas; fix rho first, then for every a, L(F_a|rho) <= L_x(Phi|rho) + gamma, where L_x counts the x-leaves of Phi|rho that survive (reused-gate leaves kept as never-restricted variables): substituting constants for those leaves and simplifying never adds x-leaves, and [P = b] costs no leaves in De Morgan form. So max_a L(F_a|rho) <= L_x(Phi|rho) + gamma is a single random variable. The selector counterexample F_a = x_a does not apply (distinct variables per a, not one common forest). Unconditional: E[L_x(Phi|rho)] <= p L (each leaf alive w.p. p, linearity), hence the worst case used by T-NORM-F (seq 17145) holds simultaneously. Correction to seq 17145: Tal's p^2 L term needs a shrinkage theorem for formulas with never-restricted leaves; Tal's theorem restricts every variable, so that term is exactly AF's open P2, not a consequence of Tal.

label: S0159
statement:
MECH-RANGE (parameter check against OPS21/Q2, seq 16795-16796): in AF with a PRG of seed s^{c+o(1)} (CKLM19: c = 1/3, seq 16757), stars >= N^{beta+eta/2} force p >= N^{beta+eta/2-1}; with the unconditional worst case s = p L, L = N^{1+eps} (D4-SIM), seed <= N^{beta-eta} needs c(beta + eta/2 + eps) <= beta - eta, so eps/beta < 1/c - 1 (c = 1/3: eps < 2beta). Hence eps(beta)/beta stays bounded for every fixed c and the mechanism cannot reach Q2 without a structural change. Two levers only: (i) c -> 0, a PRG for size-s De Morgan formulas with seed s^{o(1)}, which implies a function in E without polynomial-size De Morgan formulas (open, far beyond the known n^{3-o(1)}); (ii) a bound on the number m of principal formulas: with a Tal-type forest bound (P2) s <~ p^2 L + p sqrt(m L), Q2 requires m <= N^{1-eps+4beta-7eta} at total size N^{1+eps} with eps/beta -> infinity. The 'fundamental change' asked for by the owner is therefore a reduction of m (count of reused gates), not of W; this is a necessary condition, not a construction.

label: S0161
statement:
MMW-UNFOLD (cost of the K1/MMW route, Q-5d167697b4; MMW19 Lemma 3.1 as verified in seq 10407: size O~(N s/l), depth O(log N / log l), Circuit-Min-Merge[s] gates with l-bit input, l >= s^2; tree with fan-out 1, seq 9992): replacing every gate by a De Morgan formula of size l^b and unfolding, each input bit of a gate is read up to l^{b-1} times on average, so the child subformula is copied that often per level; over depth log N/log l the total formula size is about N^{b+O(beta)}. A contradiction with CJW20 (N^{2+beta-xi}) therefore needs b < 2 - Theta(beta): the GATE function Circuit-Min-Merge[s] on l = N^{2beta} bits must have SUBQUADRATIC formulas. NP subset P/poly gives the gates circuits of size l^a and no formula bound at all (even NP subset Formula[poly] gives only some fixed b, not b < 2). Hence the middle formula L(C_MMW) <= N^{2-delta} s^K is the R-MCSP-type obligation for an MCSP-like function at scale l (self-similar), not a weaker obligation. Open as before; it does not bypass R-MCSP.

label: S0163
statement:
MMW-M (CLAIMED; owner question 2026-11-26: does the MMW Merge architecture give the MECH-RANGE bound m <= N^{1-eps+4beta-7eta}?): in MMW19 Lemma 3.1 circuits the top tree has fan-out 1 (seq 9992), so every reused gate is (a) an output bit of a non-root Circuit-Min-Merge gate read more than once by the parent gate's replacement, or (b) a reused gate inside a replacement. There are >= N/l non-root gates (l-bit inputs cover N truth-table bits) with ~ s log s output bits each. MECH-RANGE then requires (a) l >= N^{eps-3beta+7eta} unless most description bits are read once by the parent, and (b) total reuse inside all replacements <= N^{1-eps+4beta-7eta}, i.e. per gate <= l N^{4beta-eps+o(1)}: for eps/beta -> infinity the gate function Circuit-Min-Merge[s] on l = N^{Omega(eps)} bits must be computed by near-formulas whose reuse is sublinear in l by a factor N^{-(eps-4beta)}. NP subset P/poly supplies arbitrary circuits for the gates and no such structure. So the architecture moves the whole m-bound into the gate function: the same reuse obligation (R-MCSP type) at scale l, as in MMW-UNFOLD (seq 17162). This is a NECESSARY condition derived from the architecture, not a proof that suitable gate circuits do not exist.

label: S0167
statement:
CJ3-R (REPAIR of seq 16802 / Q-88090df9cf:S0139; owner construction 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Input x then y (n bits each), n known. m=ceil(log2(2n+2)), h=floor(log2 m), budget B=m^{max(1,floor(sqrt h))}. A* runs all programs of description length <= h (K <= 2m) as bit generators P(n,i), each cut off after B simulated steps; per program an active bit and a bit d_P. Every stream bit is compared with P(n,i) (mismatch or timeout deactivates); in the second half A* recomputes P(n,i) for x_i from the program instead of re-reading it and sets d_P |= P(n,i) AND y_i. Output: NOT d_P for an active program, else a fixed default b0. ONE PASS, no random access (objection 3 fixed); m(n) and the time bound are explicit (objections 1, 2 fixed). Correctness: a program still active at the end reproduced every input bit, so d_P = [x and y intersect]. T = n m^{O(sqrt log m)}, S = m^{O(sqrt log m)}, inside the CJSW class for f(n)=ceil(log2 log2(n+2)) (any f=omega(sqrt log log n)). Every fixed deterministic generator with (log n)^c time per bit is enumerated and within budget for all large n, so A* answers correctly on its outputs. COLLISIONS: if u != v are prefixes produced by such generators, the generator of u is active after u and inactive after v, so A*'s states differ (for all large n): deterministic polylog-time collision generators are EXCLUDED against A* (unconditional). Under P=NP the PH collapses on input length m=log n, so every polylogtime-uniform AC0 generator (single bit in PH on m) is computed in time m^{O(1)}=(log n)^{O(1)} and is also captured.

label: S0168
statement:
A*-REFUTER (owner construction 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). u_j = 1-P_j(n,j) if P_j answers within B, else 0 (j <= K); u_{K+1}=1; other bits 0; v = 0^n if b0=0, v = e_{K+1} if b0=1. Every P_j mismatches at position j, so A* outputs b0, while DISJ(u,v)=1-b0: R refutes A* at every large n without simulating A*'s stream. L_R={<n,i>: R(1^n)_i=1} is in DTIME(m^{O(sqrt log m)}); L_R is NOT in P (unconditional): a fixed m^c-time program for L_R would be enumerated and kept active, so A* would be correct on R(1^n) - this is a time-hierarchy diagonal, nothing beyond the hierarchy theorem. CC(R(1^n)) = O(m^2) (at most 2m+2 ones: DNF of minterms), so R is non-uniformly easy; the sparse algorithm A** (store the <= K+1 one-positions of x, O(m^2) space, check them against y) solves every R-instance unconditionally. So R refutes A* only, not the class; CJSW's search-MCSP algorithm (P=NP) would also capture it.

label: S0169
statement:
A*-STRENGTH (director, 2026-11-26; CLAIMED). (i) The open step 'L_R in PH' implies P != NP at once (L_R in PH minus P gives PH != P); A* is only the device certifying L_R not in P. More generally any refuter R* of A* (infinitely often) whose bit function is in PH gives a PH language outside P: the route is at least as strong as P != NP, not a reduction of it. (ii) L_R is hard for DTIME(m^{sqrt(log m)/2}) under polynomial-time reductions: for M deciding L' in that time, encode w in the m-bit number n_w and take the fixed program Q='decode w from n, run M(w)' of constant rank j0; then w in L' iff <n_w,j0> not in L_R. Hence L_R in PH iff (up to the constant in the exponent) DTIME(m^{Theta(sqrt log m)}) is contained in PH - a superpolynomial-time inclusion strictly stronger than P != NP. Relative to a PSPACE-complete oracle A, PH^A = P^A while the relativized time hierarchy keeps DTIME^A(m^{sqrt log m}) outside P^A, so the open step is false relative to A: any proof must be non-relativizing. (iii) Corrections to the 2026-11-26 review note: 'P=NP gives only polynomial, not polylogarithmic time' is wrong, since poly(m) = polylog(n); the refuter need not simulate A* over the stream (A*-REFUTER).

statement:
ROBUST-GAMMA (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED, corollary of the CJW20 Thm 5.5 proof). a = N^beta/(10 log N), tau = N^gamma, 0 < beta < gamma < 1. Promise: YES = some a-circuit at distance 0, NO = every a-circuit at distance > tau. Restriction with k >= N^{gamma+o(1)} free bits (p = N^{gamma-1+o(1)}): Pr[some a-circuit within tau] <= 2^{O(N^beta)} 2^{tau log(ek/tau)} 2^{-k} = 2^{-Omega(k)}; restricted size p^2 L N^{o(1)}, CKLM PRG outputs have size L_rest^{1/3+o(1)} <= a iff L <= N^{2+3beta-2gamma-xi}. So the promise problem has no probabilistic De Morgan formulas of size N^{2+3beta-2gamma-xi}. SAMPLING (checked): t = O(N^{1+beta-gamma}) uniform positions J; NO: each a-circuit survives with prob <= e^{-t tau/N}, union over 2^{O(N^beta)} circuits; YES always accepted. So a uniform bound L(H_{J,a}) <= L_H for the partial-consistency predicate H_{J,a} gives probabilistic formulas of size L_H (J hard-wired). In t: N^{2+3beta-2gamma} = t^{2+beta/u}, u = 1+beta-gamma, which is CJW20's exponent 2+theta for MCSP[t^theta] with theta = beta/u (consistency check: no new strength).

label: S0174
statement:
PARTIAL-MCSP-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check step by step; CLAIMED, corollary of the CJW20 Thm 5.5 mechanism). For EVERY set J of t = Theta(N^u) distinct positions, u = 1+beta-gamma, a = N^beta/(10 log N): H_{J,a}(z) = [some a-circuit C has C(j_r) = z_r for all r] has no probabilistic De Morgan formulas of size N^{2u+beta-xi} = t^{2+beta/u-o(1)}. Proof check: (A) view F as F'(x) = F(x_{A(j_1)},...,x_{A(j_t)}) over N variables, A a random invertible affine map of F_2^m (AGL(m,2) is 2-transitive, so images of distinct pairs are uniform distinct pairs; A costs O(m^2) gates). (B) CJW20 Thm 3.2 shrinkage E L(F'|rho) <= p^2 L + p sqrt(L) N^{C/loglog N} holds for any formula (no AF hypothesis P2); with p = N^{beta+eta-u}, 0 < eta < min(u-beta, xi/3): p^2 L = N^{3beta+2eta-xi}, p sqrt L = N^{3beta/2+eta-xi/2} (smaller). (C) Conditional on |rho^{-1}(*)| >= pN/2 (prob > 2/3), Chebyshev over A gives >= pt/4 = Omega(N^{beta+eta}) free positions inside A(J); fix A, rho by Markov as in CJW20. (D) NO: random completion; each a-circuit is consistent with prob 2^{-k}, union over 2^{O(N^beta)} circuits: o(1). (E) YES: x = G(seed) o rho with the CKLM PRG fooling size s' = N^{3beta+2eta-xi+o(1)}; z = x o A on J has the circuit j -> A(j) -> rho or g_seed, size O(m^2)+polylog+s'^{1/3+o(1)} = N^{beta+(2eta-xi)/3+o(1)} < a since 2eta < xi. Contradiction as in CJW20. Holds for all J (not only almost all, as from ROBUST-GAMMA + sampling). READING: for beta fixed and gamma -> 1 the exponent 2+beta/u -> 3, so the target L(H_{J,a}) = O(t^{3-delta}) is UNCONDITIONALLY FALSE there. This is the lower-bound half of the decoupled route (what a contradiction needs), NOT a mechanism exclusion: deriving that false bound from NP subset P/poly would prove NP not in P/poly. The open obligation is unchanged and by DECOUPLE-ACCOUNTING (seq 17208) not easier than in the old regime. Links: seq 17204 (replaces retracted 17185), Theorem R seq 5259, QO2 seq 16796 (general circuits, separate).
PREMISES: seq 5258 (CJW20 Thm 3.2, 5.3, 5.5, Remark 5.4); ROBUST-GAMMA seq 17207; DECOUPLE-ACCOUNTING seq 17208

label: S0175
statement:
DECOUPLE-ACCOUNTING2 (replaces seq 17208; director, owner check 2026-11-26; CLAIMED). (i) QO1 (seq 16795) gives circuits N*s^K for GAP-MCSP[s/(cn), s]; its anti-checker step needs the gap. For the exact partial predicate H_{J,a} no QO1-type bound is available; t*a^K is a hypothetical bound for a gap version of H. (ii) Relative to such a bound the required circuit-to-formula exponent is e_new = 2-(2K-1)beta/(1-gamma+(1+K)beta) < e_old = 2-(2K-1)beta/(1+K beta) for every gamma > beta (K > 1/2); the optimum is gamma -> beta. (iii) e_new <= 1 (gamma >= 1-(K-2)beta) shows only that the QO1-type size guarantee alone cannot yield the formula bound; QO1 is an upper bound, not the minimal circuit size, so no impossibility of conversion follows. DECISION (owner 2026-11-26): sampling and gamma/beta decoupling are consolidated and not pursued as a strategy; ROBUST-GAMMA (seq 17207) and PARTIAL-MCSP-LB (seq 17211) stay as lower-bound facts.

statement:
CONV-D (owner weakening 2026-11-26, director check; the obligation of TRUNC2 seq 17202 in exponent form). F_beta = Gap-MCSP[N^beta/(c log N), N^beta]; under NP subset SIZE[n^a], QO1 gives circuits S(F_beta) <= O(N^{1+K beta}), K = K(a). CJW20-GAP (seq 17198; any polylog gap factor, the proof's knobs are independent) gives L(F_beta) >= N^{2+beta-xi} for every xi > 0. A problem-dependent conversion L(F_beta) <= O(S(F_beta)^{2-d(beta)}) contradicts it iff d(beta)(1+K beta) > (2K-1)beta + xi; choosing xi = beta this holds whenever d(beta) > 2K beta/(1+K beta). This is R-DELTA (seq 17161) in exponent form. Open: any mechanism for such d(beta). Logical strength: the conversion under NP subset P/poly implies NP not in P/poly.

label: S0177
statement:
NONADAPT-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED; part of CONV-D seq 17216). b = N^beta, a = b/(10m), m = log2 N, dyadic blocks of size B = Theta(b m) with a large constant. Counting gives y in {0,1}^B with CC(y) > b; x^(I) = y on block I, 0 elsewhere, has CC(x^(I)) >= CC(y) > b (restriction), so every x^(I) is a Gap-MCSP[a,b] NO instance. If a sample J sees <= r = Theta(a/m) positions of I, one equality test of O(m) gates per observed one gives an a-circuit consistent with x^(I) on J, so the partial-consistency test accepts. E_I|J n I| = tB/N, Markov: Pr_I[|J n I| > r] <= tB/(N r) = O(t m^3/N); for J random but independent of the input, averaging gives a fixed NO instance rejected with probability O(t m^3/N). Hence t = Omega(N/(log N)^3) for constant rejection. (ii) A uniform table with exactly R = C_beta b ones is a NO instance with prob 1-o(1): C(N,R) = 2^{Omega(R log(N/R))} against 2^{O(b log(b+m))} circuits. statement:
AC-FAMILY-LB (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED; novelty vs. literature not confirmed - CHOPRS Cor 61 refutes the OPS Anti-Checker Hypothesis by a different route). b = N^beta, a = b/(10m), constants beta, zeta > 0. Let J_1..J_l be a FIXED (input-independent) family with |J_i| <= N^{1-zeta}. Uniform table with exactly R = D b ones (NO w.p. 1-o(1), as in ADAPT-LB seq 17227). By ADAPT-LB (i) any r = Theta_beta(b/m) ones have an a-circuit, so J_i is an anti-checker only if X_i = |J_i n ones| >= r. Hypergeometric tail: Pr[X_i >= r] <= (e|J_i|R/(N r))^r = (O_beta(m N^{-zeta}))^r = 2^{-Omega_{beta,zeta}(b)}. Union bound: for l <= 2^{c b} (c small) some NO instance has no anti-checker in the family. So a fixed family needs l >= 2^{Omega_{beta,zeta}(N^beta)} members. Any rule using only the family's consistency bits sees on that NO instance exactly what it sees on 0^N (a YES instance), so it accepts; an AND-of-tests formula over such a family has >= l leaves. label: S0180
statement:
WEIGHTED-SUBST (owner bound 2026-11-26, director check and split; CLAIMED; within CONV-D seq 17216). F(x) = V(A(x)), A = anti-checker generator outputting t labelled positions (y_i, x_{y_i}), V = consistency predicate on T = t(m+1) bits. Substituting a formula for each output bit A_j at each of its mu_j(V) occurrences gives exactly L(F) <= sum_j mu_j(V) L(A_j); sum_j mu_j(V) = L(V). Director split, with t = N^{K beta}: (R1) L(V) <= N^{2+beta-Delta} is needed; V is an NP predicate on T = N^{O(beta)} bits, so ANY fixed polynomial bound L(V) <= T^C (C independent of beta) suffices for small beta - but NP subset P/poly gives V only circuits; R1 is 'V in Formula[poly]', supplied by NP subset Formula[poly] (OPS's stronger hypothesis), not by NP subset P/poly. Lower bound for R1: fixing the position inputs restricts V to H_{J,a}, so by PARTIAL-MCSP-LB seq 17211 (u = K beta) L(V) >= t^{2+1/K-o(1)}, and V has >= t^{2+1/K-o(1)} value-bit leaves - polynomial, consistent with R1. (R2) Given R1, max_j L(A_j) <= N^{2+beta-Delta-CK beta} suffices: every anti-checker output bit needs a SUBQUADRATIC formula; the weights mu_j matter only up to the factor L(V) = N^{O(beta)}. Unconditional counterpart (CJW20-GAP seq 17198): for every anti-checker generator with L(V) <= T^C, some output bit has L(A_j) >= N^{2+beta-xi-CK beta}; deriving the opposite from the assumption is the obligation. OPS 2021 p.23 (local copy toc-v017a011 l.1168-1172) names exactly R2 (rounds re-inspect earlier y_j) as the obstacle under NP subset Formula[poly].

label: S0181
statement:
FACTOR-WITNESS (director, 2026-11-26, answering the owner's T07-S0290 synthesis question; CLAIMED). Split the table into k aligned blocks x_1..x_k. Product factorisation (AND over blocks of [x_i has an a'-circuit]) or score folding (sum_i min_{C_i} D_i(C_i)) replaces the SHARED witness (exists C forall i) by independent witnesses (forall i exists C_i). Facts: CC(x_i) <= CC(x)+O(m) and CC(x) <= sum_i CC(x_i) + O(km). (i) VALID for Gap-MCSP[a,b], b = 10ma, when k <= c1 m: YES gives every block <= a+O(m) =: a'; NO gives some block > (b-O(km))/k > a'. (ii) INVALID for k >= c2 m: let block i be the table of an independent random circuit of size a/2; every block test accepts (CC <= a/2 < a', every D*_i = 0), while there are 2^{k Omega(a log a)} such tables and circuits of size S number 2^{O(S log S)}, so some such x has CC(x) >= Omega(k a) > b. The window is Theta(log N) components, tight up to constants. (iii) In the valid window the factorised formula is a sum of k Gap-MCSP formulas on N/k bits with constant gap, covered by CJW20-GAP (the proof's knobs are independent of the gap factor): exponent unchanged (BLOCK-EMB seq 17180, ratio invariance). MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): component factorisation / score folding with independent per-component witnesses as an exponent-gaining conversion, for any number of components. Consequence for T07 (seq 16758, A1 semantic T07 seq 16774) + S0290: the enumeration over cut assignments can be factorised only where the coupling through the shared witness is removed, which is (i)-(ii); a remaining route needs a compression of the shared-witness coupling that is not a product over components. Any realisation F = OR_{sigma in {0,1}^w} AND_{j<=q} F_{j,sigma}(x_j) (arbitrary local F_{j,sigma}) needs w >= B/2 = Omega_beta(N^beta) for q = C_beta m. Proof checked: B = Theta(a log a) a power of 2 with every B-bit table of circuit size <= a (Lupanov); the periodic tables y^{N/B} are 2^B YES instances (the circuit reads only the low log B index bits); blocks are dyadic of size >= B, so each block contains whole periods and distinct y give distinct block restrictions; a sigma accepting k patterns accepts their k^q block-wise mixtures (product of the A_{j,sigma}), none of which may be a NO instance, and at most 2^{O(b log b)} tables have CC <= b, so k <= 2^{O(b log b / q)} <= 2^{B/2} for q = C_beta m; hence 2^w >= 2^{B/2}. Tight up to a log factor: sigma = a size-b circuit description (O(b log b) bits) with F_{j,sigma}(x_j) = [x_j = block j of tt(sigma)] is a valid realisation, so w = Theta~_beta(N^beta). SCOPE: (1) block-faithful: after fixing sigma no condition reads two blocks; the recursive elimination of SEP-ELIM-LB flattens by distributivity to this form with w <= (#leaves) W_path, so with leaves = blocks W_path >= Omega_beta(N^beta / log N). (2) NOT a formula lower bound: formula size corresponds to Karchmer-Wigderson games (seq 3616), not to rectangle covers; the owner's equality example (cover 2^B, formula O(qB)) shows the gap. label: S0185
statement:
GRID-DEG check (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Setting: H_{G,q}(X) = OR_alpha AND_v X_{v,alpha|E(v)} on the r x r grid, d = r^2 groups; P = arithmetisation (GF(2) or Z) of a Boolean circuit of size S for H, deg P <= d+k. (1) TRANSFER CORRECT as a formal identity: the inclusion-exclusion P* keeps monomials touching every group; prod_v Q_v = sum_{|U|<=k} prod_{v in U} D_v on such monomials (D_v kills monomials of degree 1 in group v, at most k groups are heavy); prod_v Q_v also performs x^2 -> x inside each group and kills two-variable products, so prod_v Q_v(P*) is the exactly-one-variable-per-group part of the multilinearisation ML(H); in ML(H) = sum over nonempty sets A of alphas of +-prod(union of monomials) only singletons A give one variable per group (two distinct alpha differ at some vertex), so the result is Z_{G,q} with all coefficients 1 in any characteristic. Size (S+1) 2^d binom(d,k) q^{O(k)}. (2) THE HYPOTHESIS NEVER HOLDS - every P agreeing with H on {0,1}^n has deg P >= deg_F(H) (multilinearisation does not raise degree); setting all variables of every vertex except one interior vertex v0 to 1 turns H into OR of the q^4 variables of v0, whose degree is q^4 over every field; hence deg P >= q^4 and k >= q^4 - r^2 for EVERY circuit, of every size. The derived k = Omega((log q)^{1/12}) is implied by this trivial bound and carries no information about S. VERDICT: GRID-DEG is a true but vacuous unconditional statement; no gap shrinks. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): transfer from arithmetic state-sum lower bounds to Boolean circuits via the total degree (or degree excess) of the arithmetised Boolean circuit - for any Boolean function of high F-degree every representation has high degree, independently of circuit size. The verdict does not depend on the cited arithmetic lower bound. Route closed, statement not refuted.
PREMISES: owner GRID-DEG 2026-11-26

label: S0187
statement:
CHMY-SEED-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; owner task 'improve the CHMY/Forbes-Kelley generator'; CLAIMED). Inputs: CHMY (ECCC TR20-103, local literature/sources/eccc-TR20-103) Lemma 19 (l.718: q-state time-t one-tape DTM = sum over alpha in A of ROBPs P_alpha of width exp(O(sqrt t log tq)), |A| <= (tq)^{O(sqrt t)}), Corollary 39 / Theorem 20 (generic ROBP PRG with error eps' = eps/|A|), Theorem 47 (needs MCSP[2^{mu n}] not in DTIME1[N^{1.01}] for a SMALL mu > 0), Corollary 17 (l.657, unconditional: MCSP[s] in DTIME1^O[N poly(s)] for some O in Sigma3^P, queries of length poly(s)), Lemma 21 (oracle queries of length l and fixed coins folded into q 2^l t states); SEED-FLOOR seq 17150 (support M => some AND of floor(log2 M)+1 literals has error >= 2^{-t}). (a) LEMMA: every distribution whose samples all have CC <= s and which eps'-fools all n-input ROBPs of width >= 2 satisfies s log s >= Omega(log(1/eps')). Proof: support <= #circuits of size s = 2^{O(s log s)}; an AND of literals is a width-2 ROBP; apply SEED-FLOOR. (b) In the CHMY architecture eps' = eps/|A| = eps (tq)^{-Theta(sqrt t)}, hence s >= Omega~(sqrt t log(tq)). For t = N^{1.01}, q = O(1): s >= N^{0.505-o(1)}, i.e. mu >= 0.505 - o(1), while Theorem 47 needs mu below the small constant of MMW. Forbes-Kelley (Theorem 38: seed O~(log(nw/eps')) log^3 n = O~(sqrt t log tq)) is already optimal in this architecture up to polylog factors. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): improving the generator recursion G_{i+1} = D_i xor (T_i and G_i), or any generic ROBP PRG, inside the Lemma-19 union-bound architecture, as a route to small mu. (c) Further unconditional constraint from Corollary 17 + Lemma 21 (deterministic Sigma3 oracle machine, no coins): no distribution on strings of CC <= s fools all (2^{poly(s)})-state DTMs of time N poly(s) (the folded Corollary-17 machine accepts all of them and rejects almost all uniform strings). Hence any improved generator for small mu must have a guarantee that FAILS at q = 2^{poly(s)} states, i.e. it must use that the attacked machine has few states. SURVIVING constructive directions (not lanes, recorded for the owner task): (i) a decomposition of time-N^{1.01} one-tape DTMs into <= 2^{N^{mu}} pieces (replacing Lemma 19's (tq)^{sqrt t} crossing-sequence guesses), or (ii) an analysis that fools the specific machine without the union bound over A (cancellations among P_alpha), in both cases exploiting q = O(1).
PREMISES: CHMY Lemma 19, Cor 17, Lemma 21, Thm 38/39, Thm 47 (TR20-103); SEED-FLOOR seq 17150
PROOF:

label: S0188
statement:
JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; extends CHMY-SEED-FLOOR seq 17279 to the owner's proposal 'control the error of the whole state distribution jointly instead of per branching program'; CLAIMED). (1) What is needed is only ONE-SIDED: if M decides MCSP[s] correctly, it accepts every string of CC <= s and Pr_U[M=1] <= gamma := Pr_U[CC <= s] <= 2^{O(s log s) - N}; a contradiction follows as soon as Pr_G[M=1] < 1, i.e. G is a hitting set for the complement of M (density >= 1 - gamma). This is weaker than the two-sided 1/6 condition. (2) FLOOR for every analysis that uses only the decomposition M = OR_{alpha in A} P_alpha with each P_alpha a read-once BP of width <= w (any fixed order per alpha) and Pr_U[M=1] <= gamma: let H be the image of G (all CC <= s, so |H| <= 2^{O(s log s)} and |H| 2^{-N} <= gamma). A width-w ROBP in any fixed order accepts any prescribed set of <= w strings (one path per string, <= w distinct prefixes per level), so H is the union of ceil(|H|/w) such ROBPs; if ceil(|H|/w) <= |A| this OR is a member of the class, has acceptance measure |H| 2^{-N} <= gamma, and accepts all of H. Hence the analysis can succeed only if |H| > w |A|, i.e. s log s >= Omega(log w + log |A|). This holds for joint, one-sided, distribution-level error control (S0258/S0290-type compression of state distributions included) as long as the pieces are treated as generic ROBPs. (3) For CHMY Lemma 19, log(w |A|) = Theta(sqrt t log tq), so again mu >= 0.505 - o(1) at t = N^{1.01}. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): joint/one-sided error control over the Lemma-19 family with generic pieces. REQUIRED for mu = o(1) at the generator level: either a decomposition of O(1)-state time-N^{1.01} one-tape DTMs with log(w |A|) = N^{o(1)}, or an analysis using properties of M beyond 'OR of |A| width-w ROBPs' (its O(1) states / uniformity; by seq 17279 (c) the guarantee must fail at 2^{poly(s)} states). The transfer of the OpenAI Lemma 3.2 functional to TM transition matrices is not proved. The route uses MMW (Theorem 47), so it is not independent of QE*.
PREMISES: CHMY-SEED-FLOOR seq 17279; CHMY Lemma 19, Thm 47 (TR20-103)
PROOF:

label: S0189
statement:
BIAS-FLOOR (director, 2026-11-26; check of the owner's global Fourier error balance for the Forbes-Kelley step; CLAIMED). Owner's identities verified: (i) Parseval + Cauchy-Schwarz: sum_S |f^(S)| <= sqrt(A) for f in {0,1} with A accepted inputs; (ii) for independent D_i, T_i, G_i: b_{D xor (T and G)}(S) = b_D(S) E_T b_G(S cap T), so |b_{G_{i+1}}(S)| <= delta_i and Delta <= delta_i sqrt(A); (iii) signed S0290 convolution f^(S) = 2^{-N} sum_{u_1+..+u_q >= T} prod_j D_{j,S}(u_j) for disjoint components (Walsh characters are multiplicative over the components). label: S0191
statement:
CROSS-CHMY check (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). (0) Sign: delta_ad delta_bc = delta_ac delta_bd - eps_ab eps_cd with eps_01 = 1, eps_10 = -1 is exactly the identity recorded in seq 17297 (1) (minus sign, verified on 16 points); no correction needed. (1) Embedding Delta = sum_alpha sum_x W(x) P_alpha(x), W = Pr_G - 2^{-N}: correct by linearity, over Q. (2) Unfolded-circuit tensor network M(x) = sum_z [z_out = 1] prod_g [z_g = g(z_in(g))]: correct (unique consistent assignment), standard circuit-to-tensor-network embedding; for a one-tape DTM the unfolded network is the space x time tableau, a planar local network, so it still contains no crossings for the identity of seq 17297 to act on (seq 17297 (2) unchanged). (3) Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz |Delta|^2 <= p chi^2, chi^2 = sum_{p_alpha>0} (g_alpha - p_alpha)^2 / p_alpha (p_alpha = 0 forces g_alpha = 0 since P_alpha then accepts nothing): correct, BUT DOMINATED: by the same Cauchy-Schwarz, sum_alpha |g_alpha - p_alpha| <= sqrt(p chi^2), so |Delta| <= sum_alpha |g_alpha - p_alpha| <= sqrt(p chi^2); the weighted balance is never stronger than the triangle inequality, which itself contains no factor |A|. In CHMY |A| enters only through the UNIFORM per-term error eps' = eps/|A| (Cor 39), not through the triangle inequality; the weighted form removes nothing. (4) LOGICAL STRENGTH of CROSS-RES (chi^2 < 1/(36p)): it implies sum_alpha |g_alpha - p_alpha| < 1/6, the old obligation, so it is at least as hard; term-generic bounds are covered by JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR seq 17284. If M is a correct MCSP[s] algorithm and G is supported in {CC <= s}, then Delta = 1 - p and chi^2 >= (1-p)^2/p > 1/(36p); so CROSS-RES for such G is equivalent to M not being a correct MCSP algorithm - a reformulation of the lower bound, not a reduction. STATUS: CROSS-ID, embedding and the weighted inequality are correct and standard; they do not shrink the gap. The open step remains a non-uniform, resource-using per-term error estimate (seq 17279, 17284, 17286, 17297).

label: S0192
statement:
SHIFT-LEMMA19 (owner derivation 2026-11-26 from Viola's proof behind CHMY Lemma 19, director check; CLAIMED; model DTIME1: one-way read-only input tape, two-way work tape, CHMY l.146). Checked: (1) each work-head move crosses exactly one boundary of exactly one shift class d, so sum_d C_d(x) <= t, E_d C_d <= t/B, Pr_d[C_d > R] <= eta for R = ceil(t/(B eta)). (2) For fixed d a crossing record alpha (time-ordered, all boundaries) with l <= R entries (direction, state with current input symbol, input position) determines the block index (start block from d, then +-1 per crossing); input positions are non-decreasing, so K <= sum_{l<=R} (2q')^l binom(N+l, l), log K = O(R log(2q'(1+N/R))). (3) P_{d,alpha} simulates the block visits block by block, reading the input intervals in the order given by alpha (unknown-order read-once), storing one block (B cells), the state and a pointer into alpha: log w = O(B + log t). (4) F = (1/B) sum_d sum_{|alpha|<=R} P_{d,alpha}; determinism gives at most one consistent accepting alpha per d, so F = M Pr_d[C_d <= R] and 0 <= M - F <= eta pointwise; |E_G M - E_U M| <= eta + K delta. QUANTITATIVE (director): with B = sqrt(t log N), constant eta and q: R = Theta(sqrt(t/log N)), log K = Theta(sqrt(t log N)), log w = Theta(sqrt(t log N)), against Viola/CHMY O(sqrt t log(tq)): a gain of a factor sqrt(log N), so mu >= 0.505 - o(1) remains at t = N^{1.01}. STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE: even with zero cost for the input positions, log K >= R >= t/(B eta) while log w >= B (one block content), so max(log w, log K) >= sqrt(t/eta): compressing positions and states can remove at most the log factor; a polynomial gain needs a decomposition that either does not store a whole block content (log w << B) or has far fewer crossings than t/B - i.e. a different decomposition, not a better encoding of the crossing record. Consistent with JOINT-CONTROL-FLOOR seq 17284 (floor log(wK) for term-generic analyses). Novelty not checked; not a gap closure.
PREMISES: CHMY Lemma 19 (TR20-103); Viola, Pseudorandom bits and lower bounds for randomized Turing machines, Sec. 3 (owner check; not local); seq 17284

label: S0193
statement:
ENTROPY-BALANCE (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Setting: Y uniform on {0,1}^b, x_j = Y_{l(j)} (l surjective, Lupanov-type addressing so that CC(x) <= s for every Y, b = Theta(s log s)); M a correct MCSP[s] DTIME1 machine, accepted set of size <= 2^L, L = O(s log s); A = crossing signature (seq 17306 decomposition), R_alpha = accepted inputs with signature alpha = product of R_{alpha,j} over the block-visit parts J_{alpha,j} (cut-and-paste for a fixed blocking), disjoint over alpha. VERIFIED: (i) x|_{J} <-> Y_{l(J)} is a bijection, so log|R_{alpha,j}| >= H(Y_{I_{alpha,j}} | A = alpha); (ii) chain rule and monotonicity give >= sum_{i in I} h_i(alpha), h_i = H(Y_i | Y_{<i}, A = alpha); (iii) Z = (alpha ~ A, then uniform on R_alpha): H(Z) = H(A) + E log|R_alpha| <= L; (iv) H(Y|A) = E sum_i h_i = b - H(A). Hence L >= b + E sum_i (c_i(alpha) - 1) h_i(alpha) and, with multiplicity c_i >= r, H(A) >= (r b - L)/(r - 1). CEILING (director): since H(A) <= H(Y) = b, the balance can force at most H(A) close to b = Theta(s log s); a contradiction with a machine needs a blocking whose crossing record carries fewer than b bits (log K < b = N^{mu+o(1)}) while every information bit has multiplicity r > L/b (a constant, about 2 for Lupanov counting). Multiplicity >= 2 requires the copies of each Y_i to be read in >= 2 distinct blocks, so a machine whose work head stays in one block (block length >= its work space) has r = 1 and the balance reduces to the trivial L >= b. Generic time-t bound: log K = Theta(sqrt(t log N)) (seq 17306), so the balance reproduces exactly the CHMY regime s log s >~ sqrt t (mu > ~0.505 at t = N^{1.01}). NECESSARY USE OF q = O(1): for the folded Corollary-17 machine (seq 17279 (c); Sigma3-oracle answers folded into 2^{poly(s)} states, a correct MCSP[s] decider) every crossing entry carries poly(s) >= b bits and zero crossings give r = 1, so the balance yields no contradiction for it - any successful use must exploit that crossing entries of an O(1)-state machine carry O(log N) bits. PRECISE FORM of the owner's next step (recorded, not a new obligation): an address map l such that every O(1)-state time-N^{1.01} DTIME1 machine admits a blocking with fewer than N^{mu+o(1)} / log N crossings and multiplicity > L/b. Type: an information-complexity form of the crossing-sequence / rectangle (cut-and-paste) argument; novelty not checked. Not a gap closure.

label: S0194
statement:
ACCEPTANCE-TRIE (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Setting of seq 17306/17314: for an accepting crossing signature alpha (crossing records include state, time and input-head position), R_alpha = prod_j R_{alpha,j}, a_{alpha,j} = |R_{alpha,j}|, sum_alpha prod_j a_{alpha,j} = A (accepted inputs, disjoint by determinism). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (i) the trie of R_{alpha,j} has <= a_{alpha,j}+1 nodes per level (reject sink included), so w_{alpha,j} <= min(2^{O(B+log t)}, a_{alpha,j}+1); (ii) the per-alpha ROBP reads the parts J_{alpha,1}, J_{alpha,2}, ... one after another (legitimate: Forbes-Kelley fools arbitrary-order ROBPs) and collapses to accept/reject at part boundaries, so its width is max_j w_{alpha,j}; (iii) splitting each R_{alpha,j} into ceil(a/2^h) pieces of size <= 2^h gives an exact disjoint OR of K'(h) = sum_alpha prod_j ceil(a_{alpha,j}/2^h) ROBPs of width <= 2^h+1, and K'(h) = sum_alpha |R_alpha| 2^{-Phi_h(alpha)} = A E_X[2^{-Phi_h}] (X uniform on accepted inputs), log(w'K') <= h + 1 + log A - P(h). NEW LOWER BOUND (director): ceil(a/2^h) >= 1, so K'(h) >= K_acc := number of accepting signatures with R_alpha nonempty >= 2^{H(alpha(X))} for EVERY distribution X on accepted inputs; hence log(w'K') >= max(h, log K_acc). Replacing prefixes by residual (Myhill-Nerode) classes lowers the width further but leaves K' >= K_acc unchanged. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the trie attacks only point 1 of seq 17306 (width), never point 2 (crossing count); with the floor of seq 17284(2) any success needs s log s >~ log K_acc. label: S0195
statement:
DYNAMIC-CUT + DYNAMIC-CUT-AMORTIZED + FAMILY-CHECKER-CEILING (owner derivations 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (1) DYNAMIC-CUT: in an input-free phase, H(R^1 | R^0, C_c) = 0 (each side evolves from its own content and the crossing states), so H(R^1|R^0), H(L^1|L^0) <= H(C_c) = O(E m_c + 1) for O(1) states, and E T >= Omega(F) - O(|cuts|). Transposition r x r on one tape: F = (r-1) r (r^2-1)/3, T = Omega(b^2). (2) Two-phase check (tape holds y row-major and nothing else, then z is read column-major, accept iff z = y^T): combining the left half of one accepting run with the right half of another with the same crossing protocol (incl. input positions) gives an accepting run on a mixed input, so the left-stored bits read on the right are a function of C; from b = H(Y) <= H(C) + E[b - |S(C)|] follows E|S| <= H(C), both directions E D_c <= 2 H(C_c), H(C_c) = O((E m_c + 1) log b); for every cut in the middle half every column has >= r/4 - O(1) bits on each side, so E m_c = Omega(r) and E T = Omega(b^{3/2}). Section 6 (false acceptances, + 2 lambda) not checked in detail. (3) DYNAMIC-CUT-AMORTIZED: with the same protocol, every left alternative combines with every right alternative to an admissible window alternative, D_j >= a^L a^R, E log a^L >= H(Y_{J^L} | L^0, L^1, C) (injectivity of pi_j; log of the class value count >= conditional entropy), so sum_j (E^L_j + E^R_j) <= Lambda - b. Type: classical crossing-sequence / information-flow arguments (Hennie-type); novelty not checked. STRENGTH (director): the deficits condition on whole half-tape contents; a machine that writes every read input bit onto the tape (O(1) per bit) has L^1, R^1 containing the read bits, so E^L = E^R = 0 for every window and cut. The amortized balance is therefore satisfied at linear cost and yields no time bound by itself; only the flux bound (1) with a forced storage layout gives time, and in the one-way-input model the layout is chosen by the machine (two orders prepared once, 17325). FAMILY-CHECKER-CEILING (director, generalises the exclusion of seq 17325): let F = {x(y)} with x(y)_i = y_{a(i)} for an explicit address map a computable by a size-<=s circuit (every construction used so far: Lupanov addressing seq 17314, permuted repetitions seq 17325, grids). The machine M_F reads y, writes it and the address circuit on the tape, and for each i evaluates a(i) and walks to y_{a(i)}: DTIME1[N (b + poly(s))] = DTIME1[N poly(s)], deterministic, no oracle; it accepts exactly F, |F| = 2^b <= 2^Lambda, and rejects every hybrid. Hence every argument whose premises are 'M accepts F and accepts few inputs / few hybrids' plus machine structure (cut-and-paste, crossing protocols, static or dynamic information flow, any choice of cuts and permutations) proves at most t <= time(M_F) = N s^{c_F}. CHMY Thm 1 needs N^{1.01} for every mu > 0 (its footnote), and N s^{c_F} < N^{1.01} for mu < 0.01/c_F. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): explicit hard-input families with polynomially checkable decoders plus counting plus any cut-and-paste/information-flow analysis, as a route to the magnification hypothesis. A continuation must use acceptance of YES instances outside every such family, i.e. a family whose membership is itself not decidable in DTIME1[N^{1.01}], which is a lower bound of the same kind. PRECISION to seq 17318 (owner): the bound log(w'K') >= max(h, log K_acc) concerns the width budget w' = 2^h+1 and the count of that construction, not the width of every realised ROBP; the entropy bound K_acc >= 2^{H(alpha(X))} is unrestricted. Not a gap closure.

label: S0196
statement:
UCC STRENGTH CHECK (owner proposal 'UNIFORM COMPUTATION COMPRESSION' 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). (0) Owner's quantitative target confirmed: under P = NP, MMW/CHMY give T(N, N^mu) <= N^{1+c mu} for a fixed unknown c, so a bound T(N, N^mu) >= N^{1+delta} with fixed delta for all small mu is sufficient (consistent with seq 17325/17328: no bound of the form N s^{c'} with fixed c' suffices). (1) UCC => P != NP: verified (P = NP => Q in DTIME(m^c) => every L_k in DTIME(n^{a max(1,c)}), contradicting the time hierarchy for k > a max(1,c)). (2) EQUIVALENT FORM: UCC <=> there are j, b with P contained in Sigma_j TIME(n^b) (=>: Q in Sigma_j TIME(m^d) composed with R_k; <=: Sigma_j-SAT is complete for Sigma_j TIME(n^b) under n^b polylog-time reductions). So UCC asserts a polynomial speedup of ARBITRARY degree of deterministic time by bounded alternation; it implies P != PH. No such speedup is known (known for multitape TMs: constant-factor / log-factor alternation speedups such as Paul-Pippenger-Szemeredi-Trotter). (3) RANDOM-ORACLE SEPARATION: for a random oracle A, P^A != NP^A with probability 1 (Bennett-Gill), but UCC^A fails with probability 1: L^A = parity of A on the first n^k strings is in DTIME^A(n^{k+1}); a Sigma_j TIME^A(n^b) machine is a depth-(j+1) circuit of size 2^{O(n^b)} with bottom fan-in n^b over these n^k oracle bits, which by Hastad's correlation bound agrees with parity on a negligible fraction once k > b j (+O(1)); countably many machines. Hence UCC is strictly stronger than P != NP in the relativised sense, and any proof must be non-relativising and must fail in a world where P != NP holds. CLASSIFICATION under the owner rule of 2026-11-26: a new conditional chain whose antecedent implies P != NP; it does not shrink an existing gap; not adopted as a FruitStack target unless the owner overrides. Not a gap closure.

label: S0197
statement:
HYBRID-BUDGET + CUT-PASTE-LOCAL + GRID-LA, replacement of seq 17325 (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). Model DTIME1 (one-way input, one work tape, alphabet Gamma). Family x(y): prefix y in {0,1}^b, then K = Theta(N/b) repetitions pi_j(y) at fixed input positions, every x(y) of CC <= s, |L_s| <= 2^Lambda, Lambda = O(s log s). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (i) sum_y |L_s(y)| <= 2^Lambda, so E_Y log|L_s(Y)| <= Lambda - b (Jensen). (ii) CUT-PASTE-LOCAL: windows = time intervals in which the input head is on segment j (reads of a segment belong to its window); sigma_j = (visited interval I_j, entry/exit contents of I_j, entry/exit control and head positions, duration). If sigma_j agrees, the full configuration at window exit is unchanged, so alternatives in different windows combine by induction even when the I_j overlap; distinct combinations give distinct inputs; prod_j D_j(y) <= |L_s(y)|. (iii) Since pi_j is injective and the window run depends only on (entry part of sigma_j, segment), every y' with sigma_j(y') = sigma_j(y) is an admissible alternative; E log D_j >= H(Y | sigma_j) = b - H(sigma_j), hence sum_j H(sigma_j) >= K b - (Lambda - b) and the average is >= b - O(N^{2mu-1} log N) for b = Theta(s), mu < 1/2. (iv) GRID-LA: b = r^2, row- and column-major orders; every injective arrangement has sum over grid edges of |pi(u)-pi(v)| = Omega(r^3) (each of the ~b/2 balanced cuts cuts Omega(r) edges; this is the classical Theta(r^3) minimum linear arrangement of the grid). In the single-copy static-storage model this gives t = Omega(N sqrt b). STRENGTH: H(sigma_j) <= 2|I_j| log|Gamma| + O(log tN), so (iii) gives only sum_j |I_j| >= Omega(N), no more than the reading time. EXCLUSION (director): let C = {x(y)} (consistent tables). The machine M_C that accepts exactly C satisfies every premise used ((i)-(iii) with L_s replaced by C, budget b - b = 0, the strongest case) and runs in DTIME1[O(N + b^2)]: store the prefix y, build a column-major copy once (O(b^2) naive), then check each repetition by one linear sweep against the copy of its order (O(b) per repetition). For b <= sqrt N (mu < 1/2) this is linear. Hence (1) the transfer of (iv) to arbitrary work-tape encodings is FALSE for this family (two copies beat the N sqrt b bound), and (2) MECHANISM EXCLUDED (on confirmation): a fixed repetition family plus counting of accepted hybrids plus cut-and-paste cannot give a superlinear bound for mu < 1/2. Any continuation must use the correctness of M on YES instances that M_C rejects. CORRECTED (owner 2026-11-26): independently chosen orders cost a description each, but a jointly generated family does not: x_y(a,z) = y(A_a z) with A_a = I + U_a unipotent upper-triangular over F_2 (bits of a in distinct entries above the diagonal, needs h(h-1)/2 >= n-h), b = 2^h, gives K = 2^{n-h} = Theta(N/s) distinct permutations with CC(x_y) <= O(h^2) + O(b) <= s. This family is still covered by the checker ceiling of seq 17328 (compute A_a z per address, fetch y: DTIME1[N (b + h^2)]). QUANTIFIER: Theorem 1 of CHMY needs MCSP[N^mu] not in DTIME1[N^{1.01}] for every mu > 0 (footnote: the exists-mu form is equivalent); a bound of the form t >= N s^c with fixed c fails for mu < 0.01/c, so t/N must not be bounded by any fixed power of s, while Corollary 17 gives DTIME1^O[N poly(s)] with poly(s)-length queries (Lemma 16: N O~(s^2) with a Sigma3 oracle). So the argument must fail for that oracle machine; there, query contents of length poly(s) >= b can carry the window information. SOURCE: the owner withdrew the citation of the preprint 'J. A. Wittcop, Nov 2026' on 2026-11-26 (not verifiable); the derivations above do not depend on it. Not a gap closure.

label: S0198
statement:
MMW-SWEEP (owner construction 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: a one-pass streaming algorithm with space S and update time U is simulated by a one-tape machine with one-way input whose head pattern is input-independent (read one bit at the left end, then exactly U full forward/backward sweeps over the O(S)-cell configuration, one local cellular update per sweep pair, padded): T = O(N S U). With MMW Thm 1.3 and s(n) = n^2: P = NP implies MCSP[n^2] in sweep-DTIME1[N (log N)^{O(1)}]. This is CHMY Thm 47 (proof via MMW Thm 1.3 + Lemma 9, any time-constructible s) at s = n^2 plus an oblivious normal form. LOGICAL STRENGTH: a sweep machine with time T does r sweeps of W cells per bit, T >= N r W, so it is a one-pass streaming algorithm with space O(W) and update O(rW); conversely the construction above. Hence 'MCSP[n^2] not in sweep-DTIME1[N (log N)^{omega(1)}]' is polynomially equivalent to 'MCSP[n^2] has no deterministic streaming algorithm with polylog space and polylog update', which is MMW's own headline target (mmw19 paper.txt l.100-104: an N poly(log N)-time lower bound on poly(log N)-space streaming for MCSP[n^c] is as hard as P != NP) and the QE*/L* target of seq 10055 (G0004/G0012). It is a normal form of the existing target, not a gap shrink; restricting to oblivious machines yields no easier model here. CORRECTION ACCEPTED (owner): obliviousness fixes crossing times, positions and directions, not the transmitted states; condition (a) of seq 17318 is not automatic (the director's earlier remark was wrong). BARRIERS that apply unchanged: (i) MMW Thm 1.2 / CHMY Lemma 16 give unconditionally a streaming algorithm with O~(s) space, O~(s^2) update and Sigma3-oracle queries of length O~(s) = polylog N, and it has the same sweep form, so any proof must fail for sweep machines with polylog-length Sigma3 queries; (ii) seq 17328 checker ceiling: family-plus-counting arguments give at most N s^{c_F} = N (log N)^{O(1)} with a fixed exponent, while the target needs exponent omega(1). Not a gap closure.

label: S0199
statement:
KERNEL-CUT-RANK (owner derivation 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). K_G over F_q (q = 3): x_v in F_q^3 with sum 0, z_{e,i} = -x_{u,i} - x_{v,i}, dim K_G = 2|V|; T_G = indicator of K_G. VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: (i) for every linear K and coordinate split L|R the flattening of 1_K is a disjoint union of all-ones blocks indexed by K/(K_L + K_R), so its rank is q^{dim K - dim K_L - dim K_R} over every coefficient field (this is the matroid connectivity lambda_K(L) and the minimal-trellis state-space dimension of a linear code at a cut, classical: Forney, Muder); (ii) for a vertex split U|U' and any placement of the edge coordinates, every crossing edge forces one endpoint to lose both degrees of freedom, also when the three z_{e,i} are split between the sides (then one endpoint receives >= 2 coordinates); the endpoints losing 2 form a vertex cover, the optimum is a minimum cover, and Koenig gives min rank = q^{2 nu(G[U,U'])} (= 9^nu); (iii) bounded-degree expanders give 2^{Omega(|V|)} for every balanced vertex split. STRENGTH: membership in K_G is a linear system (3|E| mod-3 checks, O(|E|) gates; one-pass in a good order with about lambda log q bits), so the cut rank is exactly tight for cut-respecting models (deterministic communication across that cut, fixed-order ROBP/OBDD width, fixed-order streaming space) and gives nothing for general circuits; consistent with the open question of seq 8834 ('a large invariant alone cannot imply hardness'). For varying-cut sums (Raz-type random-partition arguments) the rank q^{2 nu} is a constant fraction of the exponent below the maximal flattening rank of a balanced coordinate split, while such arguments need near-maximal rank; and 1_K = prod_j (1 - l_j^2) is a product of 3|E| quadratics. Consequence: any hardness must come from the Boolean Exact-One restriction (K_G intersected with the Exact-One set), not from the kernel; that intersection is the object the next step must treat. Width theorem w* = 2 tw(G)+1 itself: Lean-checked (seq 4058, 4079), novelty question open (seq 8795). Not a gap closure.

label: S0200
statement:
EO-MULTICUT-COVER + EO-CUT-RANK (owner derivations 2026-11-26, director check; CLAIMED). seq 17348 closed by owner decision (no follow-up obligation). S_G = Boolean Exact-One solutions of F(G) = proper 3-colourings of G (one-hot x_v, z_{e,c} = 1 - x_{u,c} - x_{w,c}). (A) VERIFIED BY AUTHOR (expansion step accepted as standard): for G' = subdivision of a bounded-degree expander, every representation 1_S = sum_{alpha<=K} f_alpha(x_U) g_alpha(x_U') with nonnegative terms and balanced, term-dependent partitions (triples may be split) needs K = 2^{Omega(d)}: supports are rectangles inside S covering S; a clause split 1|2 makes its singleton coordinate constant on the rectangle; Omega(d) cut clauses give Omega(d) constant coordinates; under the colouring distribution (original vertices uniform, subdivision vertices uniform among allowed colours) every coordinate value has probability <= 2/3 and bounded dependency allows an independent subset J, |J| = Omega(d), so Pr[X in R] <= (2/3)^{|J|}. Consequence: monotone arithmetic circuits for P_G = sum_{x in S} prod X_{i,x_i} need size 2^{Omega(d)} (standard balanced decomposition of cancellation-free set-multilinear computation). Type: multi-partition rectangle cover (DNNF-type / Jerrum-Snir-type monotone bound); to the director's knowledge known technique, novelty of this instance not checked. (B) VERIFIED BY AUTHOR + exhaustive check (48 random splits and edge-triple placements on C4, C5, K4 minus an edge, triangle with tail; rank over GF(1000003) = number of restrictions, 0 mismatches; script scratchpad eo_rank_check.py): for unsplit edge triples, mark for each crossing edge the endpoint opposite to its triple; both sides reconstruct phi on the marked set B and compatibility is exactly agreement on B, so the flattening is block-diagonal with all-ones blocks and rank = |{phi|_B : phi in F_3(G)}| over every field (equal to the rectangle cover number of that cut); minimised over placements = min over vertex covers C of the cut graph of |F_3(G)|_C| (monotone in C); for bipartite G, 2^{nu/2} <= R*_EO <= 3^nu. STRENGTH: membership in S_G is checked clause by clause (AC0, linear size), so neither (A) nor (B) can transfer to Boolean circuit lower bounds; (A) is cancellation-free (monotone) and (B) is exact and tight for one fixed cut (deterministic communication = log of the block count). The arithmetic object P_G (colouring polynomial) points to the general (non-monotone) arithmetic lower-bound problem (VP vs VNP type), not to P != NP. Not a gap closure.

label: S0201
statement:
IPS-SEARCH + CARRY-DICKSON (owner 2026-11-26/27, director check; CLAIMED). (0) Addendum to seq 17359: it omitted THEOREM 14 (seq 5169, full roABP-IPS with bounded placeholder degree), Lemma 15 (seq 5174, placeholder-monomial/width trade-off) and ALG-BIT-001 (seq 3686, 3687, 3727: XOR/carry encoding, degree-2 NS/PC certificates, finite); all are restricted-proof-system or finite results, so the strength map is unchanged. (1) VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: P = NP => PH = P => BPP = P (Sipser-Gacs-Lautemann) => PIT in P => IPS certificates are verifiable in P => the prefix predicate is in P and short IPS refutations are found bit by bit (length by doubling): P = NP => IPS proof search is automatable. This is seq 17136 (E-AUTOMATE, resolution) transferred to IPS. Only one direction is available for IPS ('automatable => P = NP' is Atserias-Mueller for resolution, not known for IPS), so 'IPS is not automatable' is a statement whose truth implies P != NP. 17136(b) applies verbatim: invariants of the certificates themselves (existence, size, annihilators, dual certificates, degree) are unconditional statements that also hold if P = NP, so they cannot bound findability against all algorithms; reductions of the Atserias-Mueller type give the converse direction (automatable => P = NP). BARRIER CHECK (promised for owner step 2): the transfer relativises (and algebrises), so a proof of non-automatability needs a non-relativising and non-algebrising step; no candidate step is named. MECHANISM EXCLUDED (extends 17136): invariant-based limits on IPS proof search as a route to P != NP. (2) CARRY-DICKSON, VERIFIED BY AUTHOR: XOR part solved by Gaussian elimination (x = x0 + By), carry equations become quadratics q_j; reducing modulo the span of their quadratic parts leaves r quadratic plus affine equations; Z = 2^{-r} sum_lambda sum_y (-1)^{lambda.q(y)}, each inner sum 0 or +-2^{e-k_lambda} by Dickson, computable in poly time; hence exact counting/decision in 2^r poly(|F|). Classical (Dickson/Arf; counting solutions of r quadratic equations over F_2 in 2^r poly time); the Dickson character sums were already used in the book (seq 846, 3973, 4020). It is an algorithm, i.e. an upper bound; for an NP-complete family r cannot be O(log n) on all instances unless P = NP, which is not provable here. Not a gap closure.

label: S0202
statement:
INTERVAL-LINEARISATION (owner 2026-11-27, director check; CLAIMED, needs review by another model family). Setting: full roABP-IPS refutation C(x,y) of Psi_n (axioms = clause products Q_j of literal indicators, placeholders y_j), width w in a total order pi of x and y; I_j = span in pi of {y_j} union vars(Q_j); N = placeholders occurring in a monomial with another placeholder or with degree >= 2; p_N = max over cuts of #{j in N : I_j crosses the cut} (p_N <= owner's p). CLAIM: Psi_n has an roABP-IPS_LIN refutation (functional form, Boolean-axiom terms free) of width <= 1 + m w 2^{p_N} in the induced x-order; with Theorem 12 (seq 5128): log2 w + p_N >= c1 n - O(log m), c1 = Theorem 12 exponent constant (not explicit). PROOF. (A) Telescoping: C(x,Q) - C(x,0) = sum_j [C(Q_<j,1,0_>j) - C(Q_<j,0,0_>j)] Q_j =: sum_j Q_j D_j pointwise on the cube, since Q_j in {0,1} there; so sum_j Q_j D_j = 1 on the cube. For j not in N, D_j = coefficient g_j(x) of y_j, width <= w (coefficient extraction, as Lemma 15 (i), seq 5174). For j in N only placeholders in N are substituted. (B) Cut rank: at a pi-cut write C = sum_{k<=w} A_k(x_L,y_L) B_k(x_R,y_R). For y_i on the left with I_i crossing, Q_i = L_i(x_L) R_i(x_R) (on the cube); Moebius expansion in the Boolean values gives A_k(x_L,Q) = sum_{T subset S_L} alpha_{k,T}(x_L) prod_{i in T} L_i prod_{i in T} R_i, each term rank 1; same for B_k. Non-crossing placeholders are one-sided functions (no cost). Hence cube-evaluation rank of D_j at the cut <= w 2^{p_N}. ml(D_j) has coefficient-matrix rank = cube-evaluation rank (Kronecker product of invertible 2x2 transforms, every field), so ml(D_j) is an roABP of width <= w 2^{p_N} in the induced order (Nisan). (C) sum_j Q_j ml(D_j) - 1 vanishes on the cube, hence lies in the Boolean ideal. Theorem 12 is functional: Lemma T (report l.268-274) uses only 'on the cube the Boolean-axiom terms vanish' and the cube rank of a_D at a cut, so the Boolean quotients h need no width bound. REVIEW POINT: check that Lemma O (order reduction, report l.323-346) is likewise only a restriction of the a_D (functional), so Theorem 12 applies to cube-rank widths. STRENGTH/REDUNDANCY: incomparable with Theorem 14 (placeholder degree <= c' n, seq 5169) and Lemma 15 (t placeholder monomials, seq 5174); covers part of the Theorem 14 remainder (degree > c' n with nonlinear placeholders spread so few cross any cut). Not covered: certificates with >= c1 n - log(mw) nonlinear placeholders crossing some cut; Theorem 16 (seq 5192) shows every order has a cut crossed by K = Omega(n) disjoint clauses, so the canonical product certificate has p_N = Omega(n) and the bound is vacuous there (Theorem 16 handles it). Whether c1 exceeds the minimal crossing density is not decided (c1 not explicit). Telescoping is routine (TR26-070 Sec. 7, local paper.txt l.727-753; Grochow-Pitassi Prop. 2.1); novelty of the 2^p substitution cost not checked in the literature. Restricted proof-system lower bound only; no consequence for P != NP; M9 remains open.

REVIEW POINT: check that Lemma O (order reduction, report l.323-346) is likewise only a restriction of the a_D (functional), so Theorem 12 applies to cube-rank widths. statement:
MATROID-CUT-RANK for P_B (owner derivation 2026-11-27, director check; CLAIMED, needs review by another model family). (T1) Field F, P(u,v) = prod_i (a_i(u) + b_i(v) + c_i)^2, no factor the zero polynomial. If M (|M| = m) has {a_i}_M and {b_i}_M both linearly independent, then rank_{u|v}(P) >= 2^m (formal coefficient rank). Check: u_s with a_i(u_s) = t_i + s_i d_i, v_r with b_i(v_r) = -t_i - c_i - (1 - r_i) d_i; selected factor = (s_i + r_i - 1) d_i, so P(u_s, v_r) = 0 for s != r. Diagonal: every other factor is a nonzero polynomial in (t, d, free coordinates) (if a_j, b_j lie in the spans with coefficients lambda, mu, identical vanishing forces lambda = mu and lambda_i (2 s_i - 1) = 0, hence a_j = b_j = 0 and the factor is the nonzero constant c_j^2); the product of all diagonal factors and all d_i is a nonzero polynomial, so a good point exists over an infinite field. Over F_3 take an extension field: coefficient-matrix rank is invariant under field extension, and evaluation rank <= coefficient rank. Correct. Same mechanism as Lemma M9b' (seq 5192: diagonal evaluation + generic avoidance of the other factors); new is independence in place of variable-disjointness. (T2) Upper bound: with Edmonds' partition J (a = rk B_L[J], b = rk B_R[I \ J]), rank <= (D+1)^{a+b}; hence 2^kappa <= rank <= (D+1)^kappa, kappa = matroid-intersection number of the two row matroids at the cut. Correct. (T3) Application to K_G (q = 3, dim 2|V|), any basis B, any order pi, p = max over prefix cuts of kappa: for every vertex set S (h = |S|) a prefix cut with dim pi_S(L) = h exists; L' = {l in L : l|_J = 0}, R' = {r in R : r|_{I \ J} = 0}; S_L and S_R are disjoint (two nonzero vectors with coordinate sum 0 in F_3^3 share a support coordinate) and non-adjacent (if v in S_L, w in S_R then L'|_w = 0 and R'|_v = 0, so z_e = -x_v resp. -x_w have >= 2 of 3 nonzero edge coordinates on opposite sides of J: contradiction); |S_L| >= (h-a)/2, |S_R| >= (h-b)/2, separator D = S minus (S_L u S_R) with |D| <= p/2. Correct. CORRECTION (constant): components can still be (h+p)/2 > h/2, while Dvorak-Norin (from memory: every subgraph has a separator leaving components <= |V(H)|/2, of order k => tw <= 15k; verify at source) needs 1/2-balance. One more round on the large component (h >= 3p), else remove ceil(h/2) <= 1.5p vertices, gives order <= 1.5p, so tw(G) <= 22.5 p; the claim tw <= 15 p is not proved as written. RESULT (CLAIMED): min over kernel bases B and orders pi of the formal roABP width of P_B >= 2^{tw(G)/23} (Nisan: width = max prefix coefficient rank). STRENGTH: an unconditional lower bound for 'roABP after an invertible linear change of variables' on one explicit product of squared affine forms; P_B has small depth-3 circuits. w* = 2 tw + 1 (seq 4079) is NOT used in the proof; writing 2^{(w*-1)/46} is substitution only. The shared ingredient is the support lemma of the w* lower bound (seq 4071). Not related to M9 (IPS certificates of Psi_n). Literature novelty of T1/T2 (rank of products of linear forms vs matroid intersection) not checked. No consequence for P != NP.

label: S0204
statement:
REVIEW TARGET W-STAR (owner request 2026-11-27: definition fidelity + novelty; CLAIMED until reviewed by a NON-Claude model family). THEOREM: G finite simple, I = (V x {1,2,3}) u (E x {1,2,3}), K_G subset GF(3)^I given by sum_c k(v,c) = 0 and k(e,c) = -(k(u,c) + k(w,c)) for e = uw; dim K_G = 2|V|. For a basis B = (b_j) of K_G let H_B be the graph on basis indices with j ~ k iff some coordinate i has b_j(i) != 0 and b_k(i) != 0. Then min_B tw(H_B) = 2 tw(G) + 1. Lower bound (proof-state Q-5f55fb62c2:S0009): (L1) nonzero t in GF(3)^3 with sum 0 has >= 2 nonzero entries; (L2) two subsets of {1,2,3} of size >= 2 meet; (i) S_v = {j : b_j nonzero on block v} is a clique; (ii) S_u u S_w is a clique for each edge; (iii) |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X| (projection onto T^X is surjective); (iv) from a width-w decomposition of H_B, beta_G(t) = {v : S_v subset beta(t)} is a decomposition of G (Helly), so w >= 2 tw(G) + 1. Upper bound (S0012): natural basis has H_B = G[K_2], tw(G[K_2]) <= 2 tw(G) + 1. Lean 4.35 + Mathlib, kernel-checked (seq 4079, build audit seq 8730), public sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tonnestate/FruitStack-Eval/332a3ffeaaf6cd5ed6443fa8e3a004210fec54f4/results/PNP-001-research-graph-export/reviews/formal/wstar/WStarLower.lean (sha256 prefix dbfc812c176fae4b), https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tonnestate/FruitStack-Eval/332a3ffeaaf6cd5ed6443fa8e3a004210fec54f4/results/PNP-001-research-graph-export/reviews/formal/wstar/WStar.lean, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tonnestate/FruitStack-Eval/332a3ffeaaf6cd5ed6443fa8e3a004210fec54f4/results/PNP-001-research-graph-export/reviews/formal/wstar/Blowup.lean. REVIEW TASKS: (F) fidelity - do Ker, coeffGraph, TwLe and the statements tw_le_of_coeff_tw, wstar_le_two_tw_add_one, wstar_eq_iff encode exactly this theorem (the previous lab attempts R1293/R1325 could not read the Lean source; it is now public at the URLs above); (P) proof - check S0009 (i)-(iv); the only prior review (R1319) was the same model family as the author. (N) novelty - search for prior statements of: minimum over bases of a linear code/subspace of the treewidth of the support-intersection graph; treewidth of linear-algebraic reparametrisations of k-colouring; tw(G[K_n]) = n(tw(G)+1) - 1. Scope: the 3-colouring kernel F(G) only; says nothing about nonlinear reparametrisations or other algorithms (seq 17391).

label: S0206
statement:
SUBSPACE SIEVE for positive 1-in-3 SAT (owner 2026-11-27; owner proof, PI re-derivation and check; CLAIMED, Claude family only). Setup: weighted T41 matrix B(X) over char 2, joint Schur (17432): K = [[A,D],[D^T,0]] on T u R, |R| = nu. (1) rank D < nu => unsatisfiable. (2) Q = basis of the left kernel of D (|T| x r, r = |T|-nu), C = Q^T A Q, q_i = rows of Q. K_U invertible <=> [[C,Q_U^T],[Q_U,0]] invertible (both <=> rank Q_U = |U| and C nondegenerate on ker Q_U). Consequences: h with dependent rows q_i (i in E_h) is never true; h,g whose row spans do not form a direct sum are never true together (this also encodes E_h disjointness). (3) Char 2: det[[C,L^T],[L,0]] = sum_{|I|=k} det(L[:,I])^2 det C[complement of I]; hence with W = span of admissible rows, s = dim W, a basis change putting W on y_1..y_s: F satisfiable <=> Z(lambda) = [y_1...y_s] sqrt(det(J_s + Y'CY')) prod_h (1 + lambda_h prod_{i in E_h} l_i(y)) is nonzero. (4) Algorithm: random weights and lambda in a polynomial-size field of char 2, coefficient by sum over 2^s subsets plus interpolation in t; time O*(2^s), polynomial space, one-sided error <= (m+|H|)/|F| (only one satisfying selection must survive). Portfolio O*(2^{min(|H|, s, d)}), d = F_3 nullity of the clause matrix (algorithm R). Check: sieve_check.py, 90 random instances (occurrences <= 4): algorithm = brute force 90/90, no false positive or negative, direct formula 90/90; s < |H| in 2/90. Placement: instance of determinantal sieving (Eiben-Koana-Wahlstroem arXiv 2502.13654 Thm 5, O*(2^r), char 2) adapted to symmetric matrices with diagonal; novelty of the parameter s unchecked. Extreme case every variable exactly 3 times: B=0, nu=0, C=0, s=m=n (RX3C, NP-complete): no saving. Random RX3C: F_3 nullity 1-3 in 600/600 (n=30,60,120). No lower bound, no P vs NP statement.
