(b) Factor W = U L with L in Q^{r x n} of full row rank. Then W_j.x - t'_j = U_j.(Lx) - t'_j, so the pattern is a function of y = Lx in R^r off the affine hyperplanes {U_j.y = t'_j}. (c) Distinct patterns lie in distinct regions of an arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r (zero rows U_j = 0 give constant coordinates), and such an arrangement has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) regions (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky count; general position is the maximum).

label: S0113
statement: Cover-rank lemma (L2, CLAIMED by this session, unreviewed). Let W = P + E over Q, rank(P) <= r, and suppose every nonzero entry of E lies in a row indexed by R or a column indexed by C. Then rank(W) <= r + |R| + |C|. Proof: let E_R be E with the rows outside R zeroed and E_C = E - E_R. The nonzero rows of E_R lie in R, so rank(E_R) <= |R|. Each nonzero entry of E_C lies outside R-rows, hence in a C-column, so rank(E_C) <= |C|. Subadditivity of rank gives rank(W) <= rank(P) + rank(E_R) + rank(E_C) <= r + |R| + |C|. The lemma is exact and general; its proof is four lines. Exact check: cm-085a13b0ab7343eb (2000 random instances, m,n <= 7, 0 failures, 594 tight equalities).

structure.gap: Scope: the lemma says nothing about cost unless the perturbation support is small. It does not close G0001(i): the lemma needs |R|+|C| = o(n/log n) for the sparse error part, and no family of thr2 sharp_sat instances is shown to satisfy this. G0001(iii) (full rank) is untouched: for generic full-rank W the cover is C=all columns and the bound is vacuous. The DP corollary (rank-r DP, cm-2cd5c456ea174b3b) is a composition with the earlier CLAIMED rank-r lemma. Open: a structured instance family, or a concentration statement, with r + |R| + |C| <= (1-eps) n / log2(2Bn+1).

label: S0116
statement: L1 (sign-pattern bound, rank r): for W = UA in Q^{m x n} of rank r and any t in Q^m, the number of distinct vectors sigma(x) = (1[W_j . x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n is at most sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i). Proof: Y = {Ax : x in {0,1}^n} is finite; delta = min |U_j . y - t_j| over all j and all y with U_j . y != t_j (delta = 1 if none); s_j = t_j - delta/2. For y in Y, U_j . y >= t_j gives U_j . y > s_j, and U_j . y < t_j gives U_j . y <= t_j - delta < s_j, so sigma(x)_j = 1[U_j . y(x) > s_j]. No y in Y lies on any hyperplane U_j . y = s_j. Hence each sigma(x) is the sign vector of a region of an arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r, and distinct regions have distinct sign vectors. Such an arrangement has at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) regions (Buck 1943). Zero rows of U give constant signs. Exact checks: cm-419a6daa690544c4 (n <= 14, m <= 40, r <= 3) and cm-a34f5fbef634467a (n = 14, r <= 4, weights up to 50): bound holds in all 9 configurations.

structure.gap: L1 is a counting bound on patterns. It is not an algorithm and does not close G0001(iii) or G0002. The missing step: compute N(p) = #{x in {0,1}^n : sigma(x) = p} for the poly(m) cells in time independent of the weight bit length (the rank-r DP has state count (2na+1)^r). The MITM check cm-419a6daa690544c4 is an exact correctness check at n <= 14 with no running-time claim, so it is not evidence of a speed-up.

label: S0123
statement: L3 (closed sign-pattern count, any dimension; repairs gap (f) of L2 without perturbation). Statement: for any d >= 0, m >= 0 and real affine functions f_1..f_m on R^d (f_j(x) = a_j.x - t_j, a_j = 0 allowed), the set P = { (1[f_j(x) >= 0])_{j<=m} : x in R^d } has |P| <= S(m,d) := sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i). PROOF by induction on m, all d at once. Base m=0: |P| = 1 = S(0,d). Base d=0: R^0 is one point, |P| <= 1 = S(m,0). Step m>=1, d>=1: let P' = patterns of f_1..f_{m-1} (the projection of P) and D = {p' in P' : both (p',0) and (p',1) lie in P}. Then |P| = |P'| + |D|. Case a_m = 0: f_m has constant sign, so D is empty and |P| = |P'| <= S(m-1,d) <= S(m,d). Case a_m != 0: H = {x : f_m(x) = 0} is an affine hyperplane isomorphic to R^{d-1}. Let p' in D be realised by x with f_m(x) >= 0 and y with f_m(y) < 0. Put z = (1-s)x + s y with s = f_m(x)/(f_m(x)-f_m(y)) in [0,1); then f_m(z) = 0, so z in H. Each f_j (j<m) is affine, so f_j(z) = (1-s) f_j(x) + s f_j(y). If p'_j = 1, both terms are >= 0, so f_j(z) >= 0; if p'_j = 0, both are < 0, so f_j(z) < 0. Hence z in H realises p' under the closed convention, so D lies in the pattern set of the m-1 restricted functions on H = R^{d-1}, and by induction |D| <= S(m-1,d-1). Therefore |P| <= S(m-1,d) + S(m-1,d-1) = S(m,d) by Pascal's rule C(m-1,i)+C(m-1,i-1) = C(m,i). QED. COROLLARY (rank r): if the bottom weights are W_j = U_j.A with U_j in Z^r and A an r x n integer matrix, then the bottom vector (1[W_j.x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n takes at most S(m,r) <= (m+1)^r values (subsets of [m] of size <= r inject into {0..m}^r by sorting and zero-padding). No general position, cell perturbation or half-open convention is needed, because the argument works with the closed sets directly. Numerical check: cm-5005f106b06d4a2d (exhaustive grid, m=2..5, coefficients and thresholds in {-1,0,1}; no violation).

label: S0129
statement: LEMMA L3 (sign-pattern bound, weight-free, rank r). Let W in Z^{m x n} have rank r over Q, t in Z^m, and for x in {0,1}^n put sigma(x)_j = [W_j . x >= t_j] in {0,1}^m. Then |{sigma(x) : x in {0,1}^n}| <= sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i). PROOF. Choose r linearly independent rows B of W; every row satisfies W_j = C_j B with C_j in Q^r. Put s = Bx in Z^r. Then W_j . x - t_j = C_j . s - t_j. Let D >= 1 be a common denominator of all C_j, so C_j . s - t_j lies in (1/D) Z for s in Z^r. Set tau_j = t_j - 1/(2D). Then C_j . s - tau_j lies in (1/D)Z + 1/(2D), which never equals 0, so sigma(x)_j = [C_j . s > tau_j] and no lattice point lies on any hyperplane H_j = {s : C_j . s = tau_j}. Hence sigma(x) is the sign vector of the cell of the affine arrangement {H_1..H_m} in R^r containing the point Bx. The number of cells of an arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^r is at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) (Buck 1943 / Zaslavsky 1975; induction R(m,r) <= R(m-1,r) + R(m-1,r-1), R(0,r) = R(m,0) = 1, which solves to the sum). QED. SCOPE: any integer W of rank r, any integer thresholds, any n; no weight-size assumption. The bound counts distinct SIGN PATTERNS of the full input x. It is not a bound on the number of DP states of a prefix-by-prefix dynamic program, and it does not bound the number of residual functions of a prefix.

structure.gap: L3 does not close G0001(iii), G0006 or G0002. The DP state after a prefix is the prefix vector s_P = B_P x_P in Z^r. Its future behaviour is determined by the residual function x_S -> sign(C s_P + W_S x_S - t), not by the sign pattern of s_P alone. Counting residual classes needs the arrangement of m 2^{n-k} hyperplanes in R^r, which gives (m 2^{n-k})^r, not the Buck bound, so the saving does not follow. The table is consistent with the lemma: log2(sum C(m,r))/n at m = n^{1.5}, r = d n/log n tends to d/2 only slowly (0.92 at n = 4096, d = 1). Open: a residual-class bound for prefixes, which is G0005's clipped-state question.

label: S0227
statement:
statement_start: For integer-weight threshold-of-threshold circuits, merging prefixes with identical clipped signatures preserves the exact satisfying-assignment count.
statement: For C(x)=1[sum_j a_j y_j(x) >= T], with y_j(x)=1[sum_i w_ji x_i >= theta_j] and integer weights and thresholds, define a prefix signature at depth k by each bottom gate's status (forced 1, forced 0, or active), the exact partial sum for each active gate, and the top-level weighted sum of forced-1 gates. A gate is forced 1 when its partial sum plus the minimum possible remaining contribution is at least its threshold, and forced 0 when its partial sum plus the maximum possible remaining contribution is below its threshold. The dynamic program that extends prefixes by each next bit, recomputes statuses, merges equal signatures, and adds multiplicities returns the exact number of satisfying inputs.
proof: Induct on prefix length. The empty prefix is represented once. For an extension by bit b, add w_j,k+1*b to each active gate's partial sum and classify against the remaining suffix contributions. A previously forced gate remains forced to the same value because its new suffixes are a subset of the suffixes for which its value was already forced. If two prefixes have equal signatures, active gates have equal partial sums and hence equal outputs on every common suffix; forced gates have equal outputs by signature. Thus both prefixes induce the same circuit value for every common suffix. Merging them and summing multiplicities preserves the count of prefixes and all satisfying completions. At depth n all gate outputs are fixed, and accepting precisely when the resulting top-level weighted sum is at least T yields the exact count.

label: S0231
statement: statement: LEMMA (row-norm rank-after-deletion DP). Let W∈Z^{m×n}, C⊆[n], U=[n]\C, and let B_1,…,B_k be independent rows spanning the row space over Q of W[:,U]. Define L_l=Σ_{i∈U}|W_{B_l i}|. For f(x)=[Σ_j v_j[W_j·x≥t_j]≥T], #f is computable exactly in at most 2^{|C|}·poly(m,n)·∏_{l=1}^k(L_l+1) state-processing operations (arithmetic bit complexity additionally depends polynomially on input and intermediate bit lengths). Proof: Fix x_C. Process coordinates of x_U in any fixed order. At a prefix, store y_l=Σ_{i in prefix}W_{B_l i}x_i for each l, aggregating the number of prefixes at each vector y. Since x_i∈{0,1}, y_l lies between the sum of negative coefficients in that prefix and the sum of positive coefficients; hence it has at most 1+Σ_{i in prefix}|W_{B_l i}|≤L_l+1 possible integer values. Thus there are at most ∏_l(L_l+1) states at each layer, and the next-bit transition adds either zero or the next column vector. At the terminal layer each row W_j[:,U] is a rational linear combination of the spanning rows B_l, so W_j[:,U]·x_U is determined exactly by y. The fixed contribution W_j[:,C]·x_C is known, so every threshold gate and f is determined by the terminal state. Summing multiplicities of accepting terminal states counts all completions for this x_C; summing over all assignments x_C counts every x exactly once. There are |U|+1 layers and 2^{|C|} branches, giving the stated bound. If every selected basis row has coefficient absolute sum at most L, the state factor improves from (2a|U|+1)^k to (L+1)^k. This refines the state bound for the recorded rank-after-deletion gap; it does not imply a saving when these row norms or k are large.

label: S0233
statement: Repaired rank-after-deletion counting lemma. Let W in Z^{m x n}, |W_ji|<=a, t,v in Z^m, T in Z, C a set of c columns, W'=W outside C, n'=n-c, and k=rank_Q(W'). Let L be total binary input length. The exact count of x in {0,1}^n satisfying sum_j v_j [W_j x>=t_j]>=T is computable in bit time 2^c(2an'+1)^k poly(m,n,L,log(2+a)). Proof: enumerate x_C. Choose k independent rows B_l of W'. Express every row W'_j as a rational combination of B_l using Cramer's rule on a nonsingular k-column minor. Hadamard's bound gives numerator and denominator bit lengths O(k log(2+a)+k log(2+n)). DP over remaining variables stores multiplicities by y=(B_l x_prefix)_l; each coordinate has at most 2an'+1 values. Each transition adds zero or one column vector and merges equal states. At the end each W'_j x is the same rational combination of y, so thresholds and the top gate are determined by y and x_C. Multiplicities are at most 2^n and have at most n+1 bits. Exact rational comparisons and additions cost polynomial in m,n,L,log(2+a) per transition. Summing accepting multiplicities over all 2^c branches proves the claim.

label: S0239
statement: REPAIRED CLIPPED-THRESHOLD DP LEMMA. Let W=[P R] be an integer m-by-(l+k) matrix, with arbitrary integer thresholds t, output weights v, and target T, all given in binary. Define f(y,z)=[sum_j v_j [P_j.y+R_j.z>=t_j] >= T]. For each y in {0,1}^l let theta_j(y)=clip(t_j-P_j.y, lo_j, hi_j+1), where lo_j=sum_i min(R_ji,0) and hi_j=sum_i max(R_ji,0); let U={theta(y): y in {0,1}^l}. Then #f^{-1}(1) can be computed exactly in O(poly(L,m,l,k) * (2^l + 2^k |U|)) bit operations, where L is the total binary input length. Proof: For fixed y,j, R_j.z ranges over all z in {0,1}^k within [lo_j,hi_j]. If t_j-P_j.y <= lo_j, the gate is always true; if it is >= hi_j+1, it is always false; otherwise its threshold is exactly theta_j(y). Thus the suffix function depends on y only through theta(y). statement: LEMMA (rank-r threshold-counting DP). Let W be an m-by-n integer matrix with |W_ji|<=B, let t_j be integers, v_j be nonnegative integers, and T an integer. If rank_Q(W)<=r, then the number of x in {0,1}^n satisfying sum_j v_j [W_j x>=t_j]>=T can be computed exactly in O(nm (nB+1)^r poly(L)) bit operations, where L is the input bit length. Proof: choose r linearly independent rows A of W. For each prefix length p, maintain a map from y=A x_[p] to the number of prefixes producing y. Initially the map has only y=0 with multiplicity 1. For the next column a_i, replace each state y by y and y+a_i, adding multiplicities when they coincide. By induction, each map entry is exactly the number of prefixes with that row-sum vector. Each coordinate of y is an integer sum of p terms of magnitude at most B, so there are at most (2pB+1)^r states (and at most 2^p). At p=n, every row W_j is a rational linear combination c_j A because rank(W)<=r; hence W_jx=c_j y. Evaluate the threshold predicate from y and sum multiplicities of accepting states. The transitions cost O(r) arithmetic per state; exact rational coefficients c_j are obtained by Gaussian elimination, with polynomial bit complexity in the input encoding. Thus the number of states is at most (2nB+1)^r, yielding the asserted bound. This lemma is restricted to rank at most r and does not imply a subexponential bound for unrestricted THR∘THR.

label: S0001
statement: Occurrence-2 control lemma. Let G be a loopless cubic multigraph with vertex set V (clauses) and edge set E (variables). Let F_G be the positive CNF with one exactly-one (1-in-3) constraint per vertex on its three incident edges. Then the models of F_G are in bijection with the perfect matchings of G, via T -> T (the set of true edges). Proof: T satisfies the constraint at v iff exactly one edge of T is incident to v; this holds for all v iff T is a perfect matching. Loopless ensures no clause contains the same variable twice. Parallel edges are distinct variables and are handled by the same argument.

statement: statement: Parity-support equations for the arity-3 equality signature. Let A=[[a,b],[c,d]] be invertible over C, with columns u=(a,c), v=(b,d). statement: statement: Every invertible complex matrix A=[[a,b],[c,d]] satisfying the even-support equations a^3+b^3=0 and ac^2+bd^2=0 has the form b=zeta*a, c=eta*d, with a,d nonzero, zeta^3=-1, eta^2=-zeta, and eta!=zeta; conversely every such choice satisfies the equations and is invertible. Proof: if a=0 then b=0 from a^3+b^3=0, contradicting invertibility; likewise b=0 forces a=0. Set zeta=b/a, so zeta^3=-1. The second equation reduces to c^2+zeta*d^2=0. If d=0 then c=0, contradicting invertibility, so set eta=c/d; then eta^2=-zeta. The determinant is ad*(eta-zeta), so invertibility is equivalent to eta!=zeta. Conversely these equations and inequalities directly imply both parity equations and nonzero determinant. This closes only the parameter-classification subproblem; compatibility with transformed EXACT1_3 remains open.

statement: statement: Let A=[[a,b],[c,d]] be invertible over C. If the transformed ternary equality signature is supported only on odd Hamming weights, then the transformed EXACT1_3 signature has nonzero 000 and 111 coordinates and hence is not supported on a single parity class. Proof: odd support gives a^2*c+b^2*d=0 and c^3+d^3=0. The latter plus invertibility forces c,d nonzero. If a=0, then b^2*d=0 forces b=0, contradicting invertibility; similarly b=0 forces a=0. statement: For every finite set X, permutation δ:X→X with a_j cycles of length j, and integer m≥0, the number of δ-invariant subsets U⊆X with |U|=m equals [x^m]∏_{j≥1}(1+x^j)^{a_j}.
proof: Decompose X into its disjoint δ-orbits, which are exactly the cycles. If U is δ-invariant, then for every u∈U all iterates δ^k(u) lie in U, so the entire cycle containing u lies in U. Thus U is a union of cycles. Conversely every union of cycles is δ-invariant. For each length-j cycle, choosing it contributes x^j to the size-generating polynomial if included and 1 if excluded. Choices for distinct cycles are independent, so multiplying these factors gives a polynomial whose coefficient of x^m counts exactly the invariant unions of size m. Grouping equal-length cycles yields ∏_{j≥1}(1+x^j)^{a_j}.

statement: Let δ act on X with a_j cycles of length j, and C act on Y with c_j cycles of length j. The number of injective maps ψ:X→Y satisfying C∘ψ=ψ∘δ is ∏_{j≥1}(c_j)_{a_j} j^{a_j}, where (c)_a=c(c−1)…(c−a+1), interpreted as zero if a>c.
proof: If Cψ=ψδ, then for x on a δ-cycle of length j, C^jψ(x)=ψ(δ^j x)=ψ(x); injectivity implies the least positive C-period of ψ(x) is exactly j. Thus ψ maps each δ-cycle to a C-cycle of the same length. Distinct δ-cycles map to distinct C-cycles, since their images would otherwise overlap, contradicting injectivity. For each j, assign the a_j distinguishable δ-cycles injectively to ambient cycles in (c_j)_{a_j} ways. For each assignment, choose the image of a fixed representative on each δ-cycle in j ways; equivariance then determines the rest. The choices are independent. Conversely, every such assignment and phase choice defines an injective equivariant map. Multiplying gives the formula.

statement: Let X,Y be finite sets with |X|=m and |Y|=N≥m, and let δ be any permutation of X. Then Σ_{C∈Sym(Y)} |{ψ:X↪Y : C∘ψ=ψ∘δ}| = N!.
proof: Count pairs (C,ψ) satisfying the equation by first choosing ψ. There are (N)_m injections. For each ψ, the equation forces C(ψ(x))=ψ(δ(x)) for every x∈X, specifying C on ψ(X). The remaining N−m points can be permuted in (N−m)! ways. Thus the pair count is (N)_m(N−m)!=N!. This counts the same pairs as summing, over each C∈Sym(Y), its compatible injections ψ, proving the identity.

structure.lemma: L1 (time-invariant unrolling, exact). Let C be a circuit with s gates, inputs x in {0,1}^n, depth d(g) = 1 + max d(inputs of g) (inputs have depth 0), output gate o, D = max_g d(g). Define the time-invariant system with state sigma in {0,1}^s, sigma^0 = 0, and update sigma^{t}_g = op_g(val_a, val_b) where val reads x_i or sigma^{t-1}_h. Claim: for all t and all g with d(g) <= t, sigma^t_g = C_g(x). Proof by induction on t: t=0 vacuous (no gate has depth 0). Step t-1 -> t: a gate g with d(g) <= t has every input h with d(h) <= t-1, so sigma^{t-1}_h = C_h(x) by hypothesis, hence sigma^t_g = C_g(x). Corollary: sigma^D_o = C(x) after D steps, with D*s gate evaluations in total. L1' (time-dependent schedule, exact): at step t evaluate exactly the gates with d(g) = t; each gate is evaluated once, so s evaluations in total and the output is correct after D steps. Consequence: the two cost accountings differ by a factor D for uniform (time-invariant) updates, and agree for depth-scheduled updates.

statement: L4 (stream order, exact, bookkeeping). Let C be a fan-in-2 circuit with s gates, and let pi list its gates once each. Consider the one-pass rule: on arrival, compute the gate from its two inputs read from value memory, with s value bits and no other state. This rule computes C correctly in s steps if and only if pi is a topological order of the gate DAG. Proof: if pi is topological, induction on position shows every arriving gate's inputs are already stored, so each value is correct and exactly s steps are used. If pi is not topological, some gate g arrives before one of its gate inputs h; when g arrives the slot of h is still empty, so the rule reads an undefined value. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review. This is bookkeeping and closes no obligation.

label: S0006
statement: L5 (arbitrary labelling, exact bookkeeping). Let C be an acyclic fan-in-2 circuit with s gates, labelled in any order. Rule: at each step, among the gates not yet computed whose gate inputs are all computed (inputs of the circuit count as computed), compute the one with the smallest label. Claim: the rule is never stuck, performs exactly s steps, and every computed value equals C at that gate. Proof: let D(g) be the longest path from an input to g, so D(g) is at least 1 for gates and every gate input of g has smaller D. Suppose some gate is uncomputed at a point where the rule is stuck, and pick an uncomputed gate g of minimum D. Its gate inputs have smaller D, so they are computed, so g is ready, a contradiction. Hence the rule runs until all s gates are computed. Each step evaluates one gate whose inputs already hold correct values, so each value is correct by induction on the step count. Status: CLAIMED, needs independent review. Bookkeeping: it closes no obligation and does not by itself settle K9-D4.

structure.gap: K9-D4 remains OPEN. L5 gives a time-invariant rule (fixed program, state of 2s bits) that uses exactly s gate evaluations for ANY label order, so the D*s overhead of L1 is not forced by time-invariance alone. What remains open: (a) whether readiness detection (about s label checks per step) is charged under FB1 accounting; (b) whether the rule can be made one-pass, since it needs random access to the description table; (c) whether the stream order can be fixed to be topological, which L4 shows is sufficient; (d) the worst-case cost of the ready-set scan is not yet measured, only the pop count. Items (a) and (b) are the model-definition question the dispute turns on.

statement: LEMMA (store-then-run one-pass rule, CLAIMED). Model: a fan-in-2 circuit C with s gates is presented as a stream of s records (g, op_g, in_g1, in_g2), in an arbitrary order (a permutation of gate labels), each record read once; inputs x are available by random access. Algorithm: (1) during the single pass, write each record into a table T indexed by g; each record costs O(1) update; (2) after the pass, run the L3 worklist on T with no further reads of the stream. Claim: the run returns val[g] = C(x)_g for every gate, performs exactly s pops and s pushes, and E <= 2s decrements, where E is the number of gate-to-gate edges. Proof: after the pass T is exactly the description of C under the relabelling g, so T is a fan-in-2 DAG description of C. L3's proof (i)-(iii) uses only that every gate-input edge is counted in ind, and that C is acyclic (so (iii) induction on a topological order exists); both hold. Hence the run is correct, with s pops and s pushes by L3. Cost: state O(s log s) bits (value bits plus indices and op codes per record); update O(1) per record; post-pass O(s + E) = O(s) operations with random access into T.

label: S0001
statement: Let F be a CNF on n variables whose primal graph has a supplied tree decomposition of width t with O(n) bags. Then F has a deterministic decomposable NNF of size n·2^{O(t)}. Proof: Convert the decomposition to a rooted nice tree decomposition with O(n) bags and width t. At each bag, use one gate for every assignment to its at most t+1 variables that satisfies all clauses assigned at that bag. For each bag assignment, the gate represents precisely the assignments to variables introduced in its subtree that extend the bag assignment and satisfy all clauses assigned in that subtree. At an introduce or forget node, connect gates to the child gates whose assignments agree on the shared variables; when a variable is forgotten, OR the child gates for its two values. These OR inputs represent disjoint assignments because they differ on the forgotten variable. At a join, AND the two child gates agreeing with the parent bag assignment; the children’s variables outside the bag are disjoint, so this AND is decomposable. The root ORs the accepting root-bag assignments; distinct assignments are disjoint. Induction up the decomposition proves that the root represents exactly the satisfying assignments of F. Each bag has at most 2^{t+1} states and each state has at most 2^{O(t)} local connections, so total size is O(n·2^{O(t)}). This is an upper bound for the stated CNF class and decomposition representation; it does not imply a bound for arbitrary perfect-matching graphs.

statement: For f = e_s^T M_1(x_1)...M_n(x_n) e_t over any field F, with M_i(x_i) = A_i + x_i B_i and variables read once in fixed order 1..n: the commutative image is identically zero iff the non-commutative f is zero. Proof: the non-commutative expansion is sum_S c_S w_S with w_S = prod_{i in S} x_i (increasing indices) and c_S = e_s^T Y_1...Y_n e_t, Y_i = B_i for i in S and A_i otherwise; the commutative monomials prod_{i in S} x_i are distinct for distinct S, so all c_S = 0 is equivalent to f = 0. Consequence: zero-testing a commutative fixed-order ROABP reduces to non-commutative ROABP zero-testing (Raz-Shpilka 2005, deterministic poly time).

statement: L1 (placement, from the LIT-9 definitions, fixed polynomials t1 >= 2n, t2 >= t1): boundary-MINK^{t1,t2} YES = {x : exists p, |p| <= n-2, U(p) outputs x within t1 steps} AND {x : no p with |p| <= n-log n outputs x within t2 steps}; NO = {x : no p with |p| <= n-2 outputs x within t2 steps}. The first YES conjunct is NP-type (witness p, poly-time check); the other YES conjunct and the NO condition are coNP-type. L2 (P=NP consequence): if P=NP then boundary-MINK^{t1,t2} is in P, hence in ioBPP, so boundary-MINK^poly not in ioBPP fails. L3 (randomized version): the rK condition 'exists p with Pr_r[U(p,r)=x within t steps] >= 2/3' is MA-type; under P=NP, PH = P and BPP is in Sigma_2 within PH, so boundary-MINrK^{t1,t2} is in P, hence in ioBPP. Hence by Thm 1.2, OWF exists => P != NP, re-derived from the definitions and not from the spec's summary.

statement: S0004 (CLAIMED, not reviewed): the promise problem boundary-MINK^{t1,t2} lies in NP-and-coNP (YES = NP-type conjunct AND coNP-type conjunct; NO = coNP-type). Consequence: if boundary-MINK^{t1,t2} is not in P then P != NP, because P = NP would put NP-and-coNP into P. Since P is contained in ioBPP, the deterministic hypothesis (not in P) is weaker than the ioBPP hypothesis of Thm 1.2 (not in ioBPP), yet it still implies P != NP. structure.lemma: LEMMA W (width-independence of the P != NP consequence). Fix polynomials 2n <= t1(n) <= t2(n) and any w(n) with 2 <= w(n) <= n. Define boundary-MINK^{t1,t2}_w: YES = {x in {0,1}^n : K^{t1}(x) <= n-2 and K^{t2}(x) > n-w(n)}; NO = {x in {0,1}^n : K^{t2}(x) >= n-1}. (i) YES and NO are disjoint. (ii) If P = NP then the promise problem is in P. (iii) Hence if boundary-MINK^{t1,t2}_w is not in P, then P != NP. PROOF. (i) Monotonicity: K^{t2}(x) <= K^{t1}(x) since t1 <= t2. On YES, K^{t2}(x) <= K^{t1}(x) <= n-2 < n-1, so x is not in NO. (ii) Write YES = A AND B with A(x) = exists p, |p| <= n-2, U(p) outputs x within t1(n) steps (an NP predicate: witness p, polynomial simulation since t1 is polynomial), and B(x) = NOT exists p, |p| <= n-w(n), U(p) outputs x within t2(n) steps (the complement of an NP predicate, so coNP). NO = C(x) = NOT exists p, |p| <= n-2, U(p) outputs x within t2(n) steps, a coNP predicate. Algorithm: output A(x) AND B(x). On YES inputs A and B hold. On NO inputs A fails: A would give a p with |p| <= n-2 outputting x within t1 <= t2 steps, contradicting C. So under P = NP (NP and coNP both in P) the algorithm is correct on all promise inputs and runs in polynomial time. (iii) Contrapositive of (ii). The width w enters only through B, and B is coNP for every w, so no constant or log-width restriction is needed for (iii). SCOPE: deterministic K only. label: S0001
statement: Lemma (ring-buffer append cost). Let B>=1 and let a deterministic streaming machine receive blocks b_t in {0,1}^{r_t}, with total stored prefix length at most B bits. A state consisting of a B-cell circular array, a write pointer j in {0,...,B-1}, and occupied length q can incorporate a block of r bits, provided q+r<=B, by writing exactly r array cells and updating j and q. In a bit-operation model with binary pointers, this update uses O((r+1) log B) bit operations and O(B+log B) state bits; it does not require shifting the previously stored prefix. Proof: write each incoming bit to the next cell modulo B. Each binary pointer advancement and final pointer/length update costs O(log B) bit operations, so r writes and the metadata updates cost O((r+1) log B). In a word-RAM with word size ceil(log2 B), the update takes O(r+1) word operations. This proves that buffering can remove dependence on the existing prefix length from the append operation, but says nothing about the cost of later ordered decoding or oracle queries.

label: S0002
statement: statement: Lemma (ordered read from a circular prefix). Let B>=1 and let A[0..B-1] be a circular array containing q bits, 0<=q<=B, written consecutively from start position a, with next-write position j=(a+q) mod B. Assume none of these q cells has been overwritten. For every k with 0<=k<=q, the first k bits of the stored sequence can be output in order using O(k+1) word-RAM operations and O(1) words of auxiliary storage, with word size ceil(log2(B+1)). Proof: Set the read cursor c=a=(j-q) mod B. For i=0,...,k-1, output A[c] and replace c by (c+1) mod B. Inductively, before iteration i, c=(a+i) mod B. Since i<k<=q and the q stored positions are consecutive cyclic positions from a, A[c] is the (i+1)st stored bit. Thus the outputs are exactly the first k bits in order. Each iteration performs one read, one output, and one modular cursor advance, each using O(1) word-RAM operations; initialization and the k=0 case also take O(1). The cursor uses O(1) words. This establishes an ordered-read procedure for an unoverwritten circular prefix; it gives no bound on later computation or oracle-query cost.

label: S0003
statement: Lemma (trajectory invariance under time-dependent state recoding). Let a deterministic streaming computation have state sets X_t, initial state x_0, transition maps F_t:X_t×Σ→X_{t+1}, and terminal decoder D:X_T→{0,1}. For each t let π_t:X_t→Y_t be a bijection. Define recoded transitions F'_t(y,a)=π_{t+1}(F_t(π_t^{-1}(y),a)) and decoder D'(y)=D(π_T^{-1}(y)); set y_0=π_0(x_0). Then for every input stream a_0,…,a_{T−1}, the recoded computation has y_t=π_t(x_t) at every time t and returns the same output. Proof: At t=0 this is the definition of y_0. If y_t=π_t(x_t), then F'_t(y_t,a_t)=π_{t+1}(F_t(π_t^{-1}(π_t(x_t)),a_t))=π_{t+1}(F_t(x_t,a_t))=π_{t+1}(x_{t+1}); induction proves the state identity through T. Therefore D'(y_T)=D(π_T^{-1}(π_T(x_T)))=D(x_T). The lemma concerns semantic invariance only: it does not imply that π_t, π_t^{-1}, or F'_t have comparable descriptions or evaluation costs.

label: S0004
statement: statement: Lemma (continuation-distinguishable prefixes require distinct states). Let M be a deterministic one-pass machine for a language L over alphabet Σ, with a fixed initial state, deterministic transition maps, and a terminal decoder. Let P be any finite set of input prefixes such that for every distinct u,v in P there exists a suffix z_{u,v} with exactly one of uz_{u,v}, vz_{u,v} in L. Then the states reached after prefixes in P are pairwise distinct, so M has at least |P| reachable states and requires at least ceil(log2 |P|) bits to encode them. Proof: if distinct u,v reached the same state, processing their common suffix z_{u,v} would follow the same deterministic transitions and produce the same decoded answer. This contradicts that exactly one concatenation is in L. Thus the states are pairwise distinct, and encoding |P| states requires at least ceil(log2 |P|) bits. Scope: this gives a state-space lower bound for a chosen family of distinguishable prefixes, but no per-update time lower bound, including for search-MCSP.

label: S0005
statement: statement: Lemma (minimal deterministic streaming state count via residuals). Let L be any language over alphabet Σ. For each prefix u define its residual R_u={z∈Σ*: uz∈L}. In any deterministic one-pass recognizer for L, prefixes with distinct residuals reach distinct states. Conversely, if L has exactly r distinct residuals among all prefixes, a recognizer with r states exists: its states are residuals, its transition on symbol a maps R_u to R_{ua}, which is well-defined because R_u=R_v implies R_{ua}=R_{va}, and its decoder accepts R_u iff ε∈R_u. Thus the minimum number of states is exactly r (or infinite if infinitely many residuals). Proof: the first direction follows by choosing z in the symmetric difference of R_u,R_v; equal machine states would give equal outputs after z. For the converse, the transition is well-defined since z∈R_{ua} iff az∈R_u, and the decoder is well-defined by ε membership. This characterizes state complexity exactly but gives no update-time lower bound.

statement: Lemma (oracle-control obstruction). Fix a search-MCSP^A[s] streaming model and a cost measure u(M) equal to the worst-case number of updates, with oracle work charged exactly as in that model. Suppose M0 is a correct uniform one-pass algorithm in this model and u(M0) <= s^c for some constant c on all sufficiently large input parameters. Then no property P of update maps can both (i) hold for every correct uniform algorithm in this model and (ii) imply u(M)=s^{omega(1)} for every algorithm satisfying P. Proof: By (i), P holds for M0. By (ii), u(M0)=s^{omega(1)}, contradicting u(M0)<=s^c, since s^{omega(1)} eventually exceeds s^{c+1}. Thus at least one premise fails. If the cited MMW PH-oracle algorithm is correct and has polynomial update count in the exact same model and cost measure, no property shared by every correct algorithm there can prove a superpolynomial update lower bound. This says nothing about restricted models that exclude M0, or about P versus NP.

statement: Lemma (per-update control obstruction). Fix a streaming model and a cost convention, and let tau(M) be the supremum, over all updates of M on all valid streams, of the cost charged for that single update. Suppose M0 is a correct uniform algorithm in this exact model and tau(M0) <= s^c for some constant c for all sufficiently large s. Then there is no property P of update maps such that (i) every correct uniform algorithm in the model satisfies P and (ii) every algorithm satisfying P has tau(M)=s^{omega(1)}. Proof: By (i), M0 satisfies P. By (ii), tau(M0)=s^{omega(1)}, contradicting tau(M0)<=s^c. Hence at least one premise must fail. In particular, if MMW's algorithm is correct in the exact O* model and has polynomial worst-case per-update cost under its charging convention, no property shared by all correct algorithms in that model can imply a superpolynomial per-update lower bound. This lemma is conditional on that model match and implies nothing about P versus NP.

statement: statement: Lemma (residual distinguishability does not imply update cost). For every n>=1, the length-n parity language L_n={x in {0,1}^n: sum_i x_i is 1 mod 2} has 2^n pairwise continuation-distinguishable prefixes of length n, yet has a deterministic one-pass algorithm using one state bit and one XOR gate per input bit. Proof: for distinct length-n prefixes u,v, their parities differ for some pair only if the prefixes have distinct parity; hence this family itself gives at most two residual classes, so it does not establish the asserted 2^n distinguishable prefixes. Corrected statement: there are exactly two residual classes among all prefixes of L_n when considering the remaining fixed-length suffix positions, and the one-bit machine updates its parity by q <- q XOR b. Thus even a nontrivial state distinction (two residuals) is compatible with constant update cost. This rules out only an inference from residual count alone to a growing update lower bound; it says nothing about search-MCSP.

statement: statement: Unique-witness selector lemma. Let R be a relation on inputs x and b-bit strings w, and suppose the prefix-extension predicate E(x,p) = 1 iff there exists w in {0,1}^b extending p with R(x,w) holds is decidable by a deterministic algorithm in time T. If for a given x there is exactly one w with R(x,w), that witness can be found using at most b calls to E and O(b) additional work. At prefix p, query E(x,p0); append 0 if the answer is 1, and otherwise append 1. Proof: initially the empty prefix has an extension by existence. Inductively, the maintained prefix p has an extension w*. If E(x,p0)=1, choosing p0 retains an extension. Otherwise no extension starts with 0, so w* starts with 1 and p1 retains it. After b steps the prefix has length b, so its only extension is itself and R(x,p) holds. Uniqueness identifies it as the unique witness. Thus uniqueness removes any need to choose among multiple completed witnesses, but does not provide an algorithm for E; a resource improvement still requires a bound for prefix extendibility.

statement: statement: Lexicographic selector lemma. Let R(x,w) be any relation with witnesses w in {0,1}^b, and suppose at least one witness exists for a fixed x. Define E(x,p)=1 exactly when some R-witness extends prefix p. The lexicographically least R-witness can be found using at most b queries to E and O(b) additional bit operations. Start with the empty prefix p. At each position query E(x,p0); append 0 if it is 1, and append 1 otherwise. Proof: Inductively, p has at least one witness extension. If E(x,p0)=1, every witness extending p0 precedes every witness extending p1, so the least witness extending p also extends p0. If E(x,p0)=0, all witness extensions of p extend p1, so the least one does too. Thus after each query p remains a prefix of the lexicographically least witness. After b queries p has length b and equals that witness. Consequently, if E is decidable in time T per query, canonical witness search takes at most bT+O(b) time, excluding the cost of supplying x and any cost not included in E. This gives a precise search-to-extension reduction but alone gives no bound on E for canonical Search-MCSP witnesses.

statement: Depth-leaf bound (restricted, shrinks G0001). Let C be a fan-in-2 DAG over inputs x_1..x_n with s gates and depth d (inputs have depth 0). Its full unfolding, the tree obtained by duplicating every shared node, is a formula F_C computing the same function, and F_C has at most 2^d leaves. Proof by induction on depth: an input has 1 = 2^0 leaf; a gate v of depth k has inputs a,b of depth at most k-1, so L(v) = L(a)+L(b) <= 2*2^(k-1) = 2^k. Corollary: if d <= c*log2(s) then |F_C| <= s^c, a fixed-exponent simulation. Scope: this is the only fixed-q case proved here; it covers depth O(log s) only and does NOT close G0001, since MMW-derived families have depth poly(s).

label: S0004
statement: Restricted fan-out bound (shrinks G0001, does not close it). Let C be a fan-in-2 Boolean DAG with n inputs and s gates, every node of out-degree at most 2, every non-root node of out-degree at least 1, and let r be the number of nodes of out-degree exactly 2. Then the full unfolding F_C computes the same Boolean function as C and has size at most (n+s)*2^r. Corollary: if r <= c*log2(s) then |F_C| <= (n+s)*s^c. PROOF: For a node u let P(u) be the set of directed paths from u to the root. The unfolding has exactly |P(u)| copies of u, so |F_C| = sum_u |P(u)| <= (n+s)*max_u |P(u)|. Let R be the set of out-degree-2 nodes, |R| = r. For p in P(u) define sigma_p in {0,1}^R: for v in R on p, sigma_p(v) is the index of the out-edge that p uses at v; for v in R not on p, sigma_p(v) = 0. Following any vector sigma from u is deterministic (out-degree-1 nodes have one edge; out-degree-2 nodes take sigma(v)), and it reaches the root because the DAG is finite and only the root has out-degree 0. The walk along sigma_p from u equals p, since at each node of p it takes p's edge. So sigma_p = sigma_q implies p = q, hence p -> sigma_p is injective into {0,1}^R and |P(u)| <= 2^r. Unfolding copies each gate with the same inputs, so F_C computes the same function. Multi-edges are handled by indexing the two edges of a gate. QED. SCOPE: DAGs with fan-out <= 2 only; the bound is linear-in-s size only when r = O(log s). It does not bound fan-out-2 chains (r = s). Nothing here is known for the MMW-derived families unless their r is shown to be O(log s). Note: the statement is the standard path-count bound (paths <= product of out-degrees at branching nodes), so its novelty is only the restriction it is used for, not the technique.

statement: Leaf count of the Lemma 3.1 top tree (bookkeeping model). Let k >= 2 be fixed, s = s(n) with n <= s and log s = o(n), l = s^k, lg = ceil(log2 s), d = floor(l/(100 s lg)) with d >= 2, D = ceil(n / log2 l). Then n(k-1)/k - n(log log s + 9)/(k log s) <= log2(d^D) <= n(k-1)/k + (k-1) log s. Hence log2(d^D) = (1 - 1/k) n + o(n); for k = 2 (the regime l >= s^2 of MMW19 Lemma 3.1) the leaf count is 2^(n/2 + o(n)), not 2^n.
derivation: (1) d >= 2 and floor loses at most a factor 2, so d >= l/(200 s lg), i.e. log d >= (k-1) log s - log lg - 8 >= (k-1) log s - log log s - 9 using lg <= 2 log s. (2) d <= l/(100 s lg) <= s^(k-1), so log d <= (k-1) log s. (3) D = ceil(n/(k log s)) lies in [n/(k log s), n/(k log s) + 1]. (4) Multiply: log(d^D) = D log d is bounded below by (n/(k log s)) times the lower bound of log d (positive by assumption) and above by (n/(k log s) + 1)(k-1) log s. Both bounds follow. (5) log s = o(n) and log log s / log s -> 0 give the (1-1/k) n + o(n) form. Scope: pure arithmetic of the d-ary top-tree bookkeeping with l = s^k; it says nothing about the oracle gates' internal formula size (open, Q-4c10cf8a13 (a)), nor about general DAG simulation G0001. It does NOT close G0001 and is not a P vs NP step. Check: experiment cm-d349c1af4a9f4d40 (EXPLORATORY, l = s^2, n = 64..16384, three s-regimes): log2 leaves/n = 0.30-0.45 and rising, inside the proved bounds at every row (e.g. n=16384, s=2^128: lower bound 7168 <= observed 7318.8 <= upper 8320).

label: S0001
statement: Lemma (single-cut rank bound, B_2). For f:{0,1}^N->{0,1}, partition (A,B), kappa(A,B) crossing wires in a B_2 circuit computing f: rank_Q M_{A,B}(f) <= 2^(kappa(A,B)+1), hence log2 rank_Q M_{A,B}(f) <= kappa(A,B)+1. Proof: fixing kappa crossing-wire values gives <=2^kappa cross assignments; each fixes the A/B contribution so columns fall into <=2^kappa types, rank <=2^kappa (or 2^(kappa+1) under the K1 convention). This is a single-split bound only; it does not amortise over many prefixes and does not address D_orc.

label: S0002
statement: Lemma L1 (repairs S0001). Let C be any circuit with arbitrary gate functions of arbitrary fan-in, nodes 0..N-1 = input variables and gates in topological order, output node f. Let A be a set of variables with complement B. Call a node u A-only if its syntactic support supp(u) (the input variables reaching u) is contained in A. Let W = {edges (u,v): u A-only, v not A-only} and kappa = |W|. Then rank_Q M_A(f) <= 2^kappa, so log2 rank <= kappa. Proof: A-only nodes compute functions of a alone, so the wire vector w(a) in {0,1}^W is a function of a. By induction in topological order, every non-A-only node has value H_v(w(a), b): its input is either A-only (the edge lies in W, value is a coordinate of w), non-A-only (induction), or a B-variable (value b_j). Constant nodes have empty support and are A-only. If the output is A-only, f depends on a only and rank = 1 <= 2^0. Rows with equal w(a) coincide, so M_A has at most 2^kappa distinct rows. QED. Lemma L2 (span bound). Fix a variable order pi, let m(u) be the largest pi-position of a variable in supp(u) (0 if empty), and let A_i be the first i variables, i = 1..N-1. Since supp(u) is contained in supp(v) for every edge u->v, the edge (u,v) lies in W_i iff m(u) <= i < m(v). Hence sum_i kappa_i <= (N-1)|E(C)|, and Lambda(pi) <= (N-1)|E(C)|. For B_2 circuits |E| <= 2 size, so Lambda(pi) <= 2(N-1) size. For unbounded fan-in or oracle gates |E| is not bounded by size. Consequence: s >= min_pi Lambda(pi) / (2(N-1)) for B_2. For IP_n with Lambda = Theta(n) this gives only s >= Omega(1). Dispute reading (K9-D3): L1 and L2 use no gate-type information, so the same inequality holds for D_orc; the only difference between B_2 and D_orc is that |E| is linear in size for B_2 and not for unbounded fan-in. Both positions stay open.

structure.evidence: L1 and L2 are proved above. Verification run requested in the next call (kind VERIFICATION: independent code, random circuits with fan-in 1-4, negative control kappa_bad that must fail). cm-fc17b0e77834434e is exploratory context only.
structure.gap: G0001 is shrunk, not closed. The obligation is an order pi and circuit family with sum_i kappa_i = O(size), i.e. a reuse factor O(1) instead of N-1. Nothing in L1 or L2 gives this: a wire with short syntactic span is not forced by the cut structure. Barrier check: L1 and L2 bound communication rank, which is not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense, and a lower bound transfer needs Lambda superlinear for some f not in P. The IP_n data (Lambda = Theta(n), IP_n in P) show Lambda alone cannot give that. Not a P vs NP progress claim.

statement: Lemma A (indicator degree): for Z subset {0,1}^t, deg_F2(1_Z) = t iff |Z| is odd (top ANF coefficient = |Z| mod 2). Lemma A' (Reed-Muller weight): a nonzero multilinear F2 polynomial of degree d has at least 2^(t-d) nonzero points, so deg_F2(1_Z) >= t - log2|Z| for nonempty Z. Lemma B (repair): for any encoding E: {0,1}^t -> {0,1}^S with component degrees d_j and zero class Z0 = E^{-1}(E(0^t)), sum_j d_j >= t - log2|Z0|. Proof: P(x) = prod_j (1+E_j(x)+E_j(0^t)) equals 1_{Z0}(x); deg P <= sum_j d_j; deg 1_{Z0} >= t - log2|Z0| by A'. Consequences: sum_j d_j >= t when Z0 = {0^t} (the original sketch) and when |Z0| is odd (Lemma A).

label: S0002
statement: L-GF3: For a positive 1-in-3 CNF F on variables 0..n-1 (3 distinct variables per clause) with incidence matrix A over GF(3) and V = {x in F_3^n : Ax = 1 mod 3}: (1) F is satisfiable iff V contains a 0/1 point; (2) if V is nonempty then |V| = 3^(n - rank_3 A), and if V is empty then F is unsatisfiable; (3) hence #SAT(F) <= 3^(n - rank_3 A). Proof: (1) a 1-in-3 solution gives clause sums exactly 1, so Ax = 1 mod 3; conversely a 0/1 point with every clause sum = 1 mod 3 has clause sums in {0,1,2,3} congruent to 1, hence equal to 1. (2) Gaussian elimination over F_3 on [A|1] gives V = x0 + ker A, dim ker A = n - rank_3 A. (3) follows from (1) and (2). Scope: restates S0001 (same claim, same scope). Not a speed-up: it beats 2^n only when rank_3 A > (1 - log_3 2) n, about 0.369 n. Finite check cm-40b8f023cf164326 (360 instances, n=6..9) matches the claim but is not a proof.

label: S0003
statement: LEMMA (all-ones kernel). For a positive 1-in-3 CNF F on variables 0..n-1 with exactly 3 distinct variables per clause and incidence matrix A in {0,1}^{m x n}: A*1 = 0 mod 3 (each row sums to 3), so 1 lies in ker_3 A, rank_3 A <= n-1, and k := n - rank_3 A >= 1 for every instance. The affine set V = {x : Ax = 1 mod 3}, if nonempty, is closed under x -> x+1. Proof: each row of A has exactly three entries 1, so (A1)_i = 3 = 0 mod 3. Consequence (REPAIR of the generic-rank formula in S0001/S0002): k = max(0, n-m) is false for m near or above n; the true k is >= 1. The exponent threshold k < 0.631n is unchanged, so this is a constant-level correction, not a speed-up. Scope: positive 1-in-3, 3-uniform clauses. Discovery cm-f6bb3e59767d4efd: H0 (rank = min(m,n)) is refuted for m >= n-1 (deficiency 40/40 at m=n, mean k about 1 for m >= n); H1 (clause dependencies) is confirmed; decision mismatch 0 in all cases.

label: S0003
statement: PROOF. Distinct rows of M are 0/1 vectors in V, so they lie in V and the bound is |V ∩ {0,1}^n| <= 2^r. Let B be an r x n matrix whose rows are a basis of V. B has rank r, so it has r linearly independent columns; let S be their index set, |S| = r. For v = cB in V (c in Q^r), v_S = c B_S, and B_S is invertible, so c is determined by v_S and hence v is determined by v_S. So the restriction x -> x_S is injective on V. It maps V ∩ {0,1}^n into {0,1}^S, which has 2^r elements. Hence |V ∩ {0,1}^n| <= 2^r. For the corollary: fix an order pi that attains W_rank. Every cut k has distinct-row count <= 2^{rank_k} <= 2^{W_rank}, so the max over cuts is <= 2^{W_rank}; minimising over orders gives W_OBDD <= 2^{W_rank}. Check: F={x0+x1+x2=1} has W_rank=2, W_OBDD=3 <= 4. The lemma is elementary and is probably standard in the rank-versus-OBDD literature; it is recorded as a verified finite-scope step, not as new. CLAIMED until reviewed by another session.

label: S0007
statement: SHARPNESS LEMMA (linear algebra, not a lower bound; barrier check: not applicable, no complexity claim). Let MUX_r on n=r+s variables (s=ceil(log2 r)) be f(d,sel)=d[sel mod r], and take the cut after the r data variables. Rows are indexed by d in {0,1}^r and the row is A d, where A is a 2^s x r 0/1 matrix with A[sel,i]=[sel mod r = i]. Each column i of A is nonzero (sel=i, valid since i<r<=2^s) and the columns have disjoint supports, so A has rank r over Q, hence d -> A d is injective. Therefore the cut has exactly 2^r distinct rows and Q-rank r, i.e. #distinct = 2^{rank_Q} holds with equality for every r>=1. Consequence: the per-cut bound of S0003 cannot be improved in general; any improvement of W_OBDD <= 2^{W_rank} must use the minimum over orders. Scope: all r>=1; exact check for r=2,3,4 in cm-efdd80a50098468a.

label: S0009
statement: LEMMA (chain CNF, natural order): for every n >= 3 and every cut k, the number of distinct residual functions of C_n in the natural order is at most 5. Proof: the prefix constraints are all checked by the prefix; the only clauses crossing the cut contain x_{k-2}, x_{k-1} (prefix) and x_k (suffix). The residual is 0 if the prefix violates a clause, and otherwise depends only on the pair (x_{k-2}, x_{k-1}) (4 possibilities). Total at most 5. Status: CLAIMED until reviewed by another session.

statement: Subspace bound: for a rational subspace V of Q^N with dim V = r, |V ∩ {0,1}^N| <= 2^r. Hence for any Boolean f and cut k, D_k <= 2^{rank_Q(cut k)}, so W_OBDD(order) <= 2^{W_rank} for every f and every order. Closes G0002 in general (stronger than the satisfiable positive 1-in-3 scope). label: S0023
statement: LEMMA (rank sandwich for OBDD width). Let f:{0,1}^n->{0,1}, let pi be a variable order, and for 1<=l<=n-1 let M_l(f,pi) be the 0/1 matrix with rows indexed by assignments a to the first l variables, columns by assignments b to the remaining variables, entries f(a,b). Let R_l = rank over GF(2) of M_l, and D_l = number of DISTINCT rows of M_l (= number of distinct subfunctions f|_a). Then R_l <= D_l <= 2^{R_l}. Consequently minRank(f) <= min_pi max_l D_l(f,pi) <= 2^{minRank(f)}, where minRank(f) = min_pi max_l R_l(f,pi). PROOF. Let V be the GF(2) row space of M_l, dim V = R_l, so |V| = 2^{R_l}. Every row lies in V, and the rows span V by definition, so the set of distinct rows is a spanning set of V; hence D_l >= R_l. Also the distinct rows are elements of V, so D_l <= |V| = 2^{R_l}. For the consequence: for each pi, max_l R_l <= max_l D_l, so minRank <= min_pi max_l D_l. For pi* attaining minRank, max_l D_l(f,pi*) <= 2^{max_l R_l(f,pi*)} = 2^{minRank}, so min_pi max_l D_l <= 2^{minRank}. Each step is elementary linear algebra over GF(2); no computation is used. SCOPE: all Boolean f, all n>=2, all orders. STATUS OF THE GAP: this sandwich is two-sided but does not decide G0001. The lower side is trivial (D >= R). The upper side gives only the exponential relation, not the reverse direction that G0001 asks for. It is not a P vs NP claim and carries no barrier content (no lower bound is proved).

label: S0024
statement: Proof: write A = sum_{i<=r} u_i v_i^T and B = sum_{j<=s} x_j y_j^T with r=rank A, s=rank B. Then (u_i v_i^T) o (x_j y_j^T) = (u_i o x_j)(v_i o y_j)^T, so A o B = sum_{i,j} (u_i o x_j)(v_i o y_j)^T, a sum of r*s rank-one matrices. The cut-matrix consequence uses that the cut matrix of f AND g is the entrywise product of the cut matrices of f and g. Status: CLAIMED; the lemma is elementary (classical Schur-product rank bound) and is recorded for bookkeeping, not as new mathematics.

label: S0026
statement: Proof: an assignment x falsifies C_i for all i in S iff, for each literal l in C_i, x makes l false; so the set of such x is {x : x agrees with the forced values of S}. If the forced values conflict, the set is empty; if consistent, it is a subcube fixing exactly |V(S)| variables, of size 2^(n-|V(S)|). Inclusion-exclusion over the falsified-clause events A_i = {x falsifies C_i} gives #(no A_i) = sum_S (-1)^|S| |intersection_{i in S} A_i|, which is the formula. Clauses with complementary literals are never falsified and are handled by the conflict case. Status: CLAIMED, the argument is elementary and standard; the value is a precise statement, not new mathematics. The sum has 2^m terms, so it gives no polynomial-time algorithm.

structure.lemma: S-54f648a904 (formal). Let F = C_1 AND ... AND C_m be a CNF on variables 0..n-1, each clause a set of literals. For S subset of {1..m} let V(S) be the set of variables occurring in clauses of S, and say S is consistent if the assignments that falsify every literal of every clause in S exist, i.e. no variable is required both 0 and 1. Then #F = sum_{S} (-1)^|S| N(S), with N(S) = 2^(n - |V(S)|) if S is consistent and N(S) = 0 otherwise.

structure.lemma: REPAIR R1 of S-fa5d8faae8. Let F be a field, M an m x k matrix over F, and d(M) the number of distinct rows of M in F^k. Then rank_F(M) <= d(M). Proof: the row space of M is spanned by its m rows; a repeated row contributes nothing new to the span, so the row space is spanned by the d(M) distinct rows and has dimension at most d(M). Strictness: rows (1,0),(0,1),(1,1) over Q or GF(2) give d = 3 and rank = 2. So the literal reading 'number of classes = rank' is false, and the field-valued rank rank_F(M) (with F named explicitly) is the correct count for a grouping that works over a fixed field.

label: S0038
statement: L-HWB-RANK (CLAIMED, derived in session R1498; needs review by another model family). Setup: HWB_n(x)=x_{|x|} for |x|>=1, 0 for |x|=0. Fix p in {0..n}, a=(x_1..x_p), b=(x_{p+1}..x_n), M_p[a,b]=HWB_n(a,b). Claim: rank_Q(M_p) <= (p+1)^2 <= (n+1)^2. Proof: HWB(x)=sum_{t=1}^n [|x|=t] x_t. Put s=|a|. For t<=p the term is a_t [|b|=t-s]; for t>p it is [|b|=t-s] b_{t-p}. So row a equals F_s(b) + sum_{t=1}^p a_t H_{t-s}(b), with s=|a|, H_u(b)=[|b|=u], F_s(b)=sum_{t=p+1}^n [|b|=t-s] b_{t-p}. Each row lies in V_s = span{F_s, H_{t-s}: 1<=t<=p}, dim <= p+1, and V_s depends only on s in {0..p}. So the row space lies in sum_{s=0}^p V_s, of dimension <= (p+1)^2. Consequence (conditional on H below): the natural order gives W_rank(HWB_n) <= (n+1)^2, so min over orders is <= (n+1)^2. H (CITED, NOT VERIFIED AT SOURCE; secondary arXiv 1912.01430 Prop. 4 proof attributes it to Bryant [10] with an improvement in Wegener's book Thm 4.10.2): every OBDD for HWB_n, for every variable order, has size >= 2^{n/5}. Then max level width >= (2^{n/5}-2)/(n+1), so W_OBDD(HWB_n) >= 2^{Omega(sqrt(W_rank))}, which refutes any polynomial bound W_OBDD <= poly(W_rank) on the HWB family, conditional on H. Scope: the rank bound is unconditional for all n and all p; the separation is conditional on H.

label: S0039
statement: Proof. Rows of M lie in V = rowspace_F(M), dim V = r. Distinct rows span V, so D >= r. Let B be an r x N matrix whose rows form a basis of V, and S a set of r columns with B_S invertible over F. For v = cB in V, v_S = c B_S, so v is determined by v_S; restriction to S is injective on V. Distinct 0/1 rows of M are distinct elements of V whose restrictions lie in {0,1}^S, a set of 2^r elements, so D <= 2^r. The order consequence follows by applying this to each cut, since distinct subfunctions at a cut equal distinct rows of its cut matrix.

label: S0041
statement: S-AND-WIDTH-01: Let F, G: {0,1}^k -> {0,1} be Boolean functions on the same prefix-cut, with residual functions f_a = F(a, .) and g_a = G(a, .) over the suffix variables, and D(H) = number of distinct residual functions of H over prefixes a. Then D(F AND G) <= D(F) D(G). If in addition the zero residual occurs among the residuals of both F and G, then D(F AND G) <= 1 + (D(F)-1)(D(G)-1). Proof: the residual of F AND G at a is f_a AND g_a, so D(F AND G) is at most the number of distinct pairs (f_a, g_a), giving the product bound. For the sharpened bound, a nonzero residual f_a AND g_a forces f_a and g_a nonzero, so the nonzero residuals of F AND G lie in {u AND v : u in N_F, v in N_G}, where N_F is the set of nonzero residuals of F, and |N_F| = D(F)-1 when zero is a residual of F (likewise G). This gives at most (D(F)-1)(D(G)-1) nonzero residuals plus one zero residual. Scope: finite Boolean functions with a fixed variable cut; this is a width bound for pointwise AND of residual sets, not a bound on any algorithm's running time.

statement: S-sandwich-rank-OBDD (LEMMA, CLAIMED). Scope: any Boolean f on {0,1}^n, any variable order, any cut k. Let M_k be the 2^k x 2^(n-k) matrix M_k[a,b] = f(a,b) with prefix a and suffix b. Let D_k = number of distinct rows of M_k and R_k = rank over Q of M_k. Claim: R_k <= D_k <= 2^(R_k). Proof. (i) The D_k distinct rows span the row space of M_k, which contains all rows, so R_k <= D_k. (ii) Let V be the row space of M_k, dim V = R_k. Choose R_k columns S on which the projection x -> x_S is injective on V (a basis matrix of V has R_k independent columns). The distinct rows are distinct elements of V in {0,1}^(2^(n-k)), so their restrictions to S are pairwise distinct and lie in {0,1}^S, which has 2^(R_k) elements. Hence D_k <= 2^(R_k). Consequence: write W_rank(pi) = max_k R_k and W_OBDD(pi) = max_k D_k. For every order pi, W_rank(pi) <= W_OBDD(pi) <= 2^(W_rank(pi)); minimising over pi gives min_pi W_rank <= min_pi W_OBDD <= 2^(min_pi W_rank). Gap relation: G0001 asks whether min_pi W_OBDD <= poly(min_pi W_rank). The sandwich reduces G0001 to whether the factor 2^(W_rank) can be replaced by a polynomial in the minimum-over-orders setting; it does not close G0001. Per-cut tightness: the MUX cut of S0007 has D = 2^R, so no per-order polynomial improvement exists; only the minimum over orders can help. statement:
statement: For every n >= 2, every order of the n variables and every cut with prefix set A (|A| = k): rank_Q(M_A) <= (k+1)(n-k+1) <= floor((n+2)^2/4), where M_A is the cut matrix of HWB_n(x) = x_{|x|} (0 if |x| = 0) with rows indexed by prefix assignments a and columns by suffix assignments b.
proof: Split rows of M_A by the weight s in {0..k} of a and columns by the weight t in {0..n-k} of b. This gives (k+1)(n-k+1) blocks R_{s,t}, and M_A is the sum of their zero-padded versions. On R_{s,t}, |a union b| = s+t = j is constant, so the entry equals x_j for a fixed variable j. If j = 0 the block is zero. If j in A, the entry is a_j, which depends only on the row, so the block has rank <= 1. If j in B, the entry is b_j, which depends only on the column, so the block has rank <= 1. Rank is subadditive, so rank_Q(M_A) <= (k+1)(n-k+1). Maximising over k gives floor((n+2)^2/4).
shrinks: G0001 rank side for HWB_n: W_rank(HWB_n) <= floor((n+2)^2/4) for every order. Does not supply the superpolynomial min-over-orders OBDD width lower bound.

label: S0044
statement:
statement: Let M be a matrix over Q with k columns and r = rank_Q(M). The number of distinct 0/1 rows of M is at most 2^r. Consequently, for a fixed variable order, the number of distinct residual functions at a cut is at most 2^{rank_Q(M_cut)}. Scope: fixed order only; min over orders is NOT covered (G0001 stays open).
proof: Let V = rowspace(M), dim V = r. Choose r columns J with a nonzero r x r minor. The projection pi_J: V -> Q^J has image of dimension rank(M restricted to J) = r, so it is injective on V. Each distinct 0/1 row lies in V and maps injectively into {0,1}^J, which has 2^r elements. The GF(2) inequality rank_GF2(M) <= rank_Q(M) holds because a minor nonzero mod 2 is nonzero over Q.

label: S0045
statement: BUCKET-ELIM-EXACT (standard, Dechter 1999; recorded as bookkeeping, closes no obligation). Let F(x_1..x_n) = prod_{i=1..k} f_i(x_{S_i}) with f_i : {0,1}^{S_i} -> Z_{>=0}. Fix an order v_1..v_n. At step t, let I_t be the factors whose scope contains v_t, U_t the union of their scopes, and g_t(x_{U_t \ {v_t}}) = sum_{x_{v_t} in {0,1}} prod_{i in I_t} f_i. Then (a) the sum of F over {0,1}^n equals the value of the final scalar product obtained by the recursion (distributivity of product over sum, since v_t occurs only in the factors of I_t at step t); (b) the product table at step t has 2^{|U_t|} entries and g_t has 2^{|U_t|-1} entries; (c) so the largest table is at most 2^{w+1}, w = max_t (|U_t| - 1). Proof: (a) induction on t, using that v_t occurs in no factor outside I_t at that point; (b) by definition of U_t. Scope: finite Boolean, nonnegative weights, any fixed order. Consequence: exact counting for positive 1-in-3 CNF costs sum_t 2^{|U_t|} arithmetic operations, with the 3-variable clause table having 3 of 8 entries nonzero.

label: S0046
statement:
statement: Let M be a 0/1 matrix over Q with rank_Q(M) = r. Then M has at most 2^r distinct rows. Consequently, for a fixed variable order and cut k, the number of distinct residual functions D_k <= 2^{r_k}, where r_k = rank_Q of the cut communication matrix, and the OBDD width of that order is <= 2^{max_k r_k}.
derivation: Let V in Q^B be the row space of M, dim V = r. Choose a basis of V, form the r x |B| matrix of basis vectors, and pick r columns J on which it is invertible. The projection pi_J: V -> Q^J is then injective. Every row of M lies in V and has entries in {0,1}, so pi_J(row) lies in {0,1}^J, which has 2^r elements. Hence a row is determined by at most 2^r values and M has at most 2^r distinct rows. Applying this to the cut matrix of each level k gives D_k <= 2^{r_k}. Scope: this is an exponential bound 2^{O(W_rank)} only; it does not give the polynomial form poly(W_rank) asked in the gap.

label: S0047
statement:
statement: For every r >= 1 there is a 0/1 matrix M_r with rank_Q(M_r) = r and exactly 2^r distinct rows, so the bound 'distinct rows <= 2^{rank_Q}' of S0046 is tight for arbitrary 0/1 matrices.
derivation: Index rows by x in {0,1}^r and columns by j in [r], with M_r[x,j] = x_j. The rows x = e_i (unit vectors) are the standard basis of Q^r, so rank_Q(M_r) = r (at most r columns, and r independent rows). The row indexed by x equals x itself, so the rows are pairwise distinct and there are 2^r of them. Scope: arbitrary 0/1 matrices. Not claimed: that M_r is a cut matrix of any formula or THR o THR circuit of size poly(r). Consequence: closing G0001 (poly form) needs a property of cut matrices of bounded-size circuits beyond their rank.

label: S0050
statement:
statement: Let F: {0,1}^n -> {0,1} and let S be a set of variables. Let M_S be the cut matrix with rows indexed by assignments to S, columns by assignments to the complement, and entries F. Let K(S) be the number of distinct rows of M_S and R(S) the rank over Q of M_S. Then K(S) <= 2^R(S). Consequently W(F) <= 2^R(F), where W(F) is the min over variable orders of the max over prefixes of K, and R(F) is the min over orders of the max over prefixes of R.
proof: Let r = R(S) and let V be the row space of M_S over Q, so dim V = r. Choose r linearly independent columns J of M_S. Since these columns span the column space, the submatrix M_S[:,J] has rank r, so its row space has dimension r. That row space is the image of V under the projection p_J to Q^J, so p_J is injective on V. Each distinct row of M_S is a distinct 0/1 vector lying in V, so distinct rows have distinct restrictions to J, and those restrictions lie in {0,1}^J, a set of size 2^r. Hence K(S) <= 2^r. For the consequence, take an order pi minimising the max over prefixes of R. Then the max over prefixes of K is at most 2^(max R), so W(F) <= 2^R(F). Tightness: for rows x in {0,1}^r and columns j in [r], with M[x,j] = x_j, the rank is r and K = 2^r, so the bound is attained. Scope: arbitrary Boolean functions, any n. This is the multiplicative repair of H_A and is exponential, so it does not yet give a polynomial width bound.

label: S0051
statement:
statement: Let F = AND of factors f_1..f_m on Boolean variables, each factor on at most 3 variables. For a variable set S let dS be the set of variables in S that occur in a factor which also contains a variable outside S. Let K(S) be the number of distinct residual functions of F on the complement, indexed by assignments to S. Then K(S) <= 2^|dS| + 1.
proof: Split factors into I (inside S), J (crossing), O (inside complement). For prefix assignment a, the residual is g(a) AND h(b) AND over f in J of f(a restricted to S cap f, b), where g(a) = AND over I of f(a) and h(b) = AND over O of f(b) does not depend on a. Each crossing factor depends on a only through a restricted to dS. So the residual is determined by the pair (g(a), a restricted to dS). If g(a)=0 the residual is the zero function (one residual). If g(a)=1 it is determined by a restricted to dS, at most 2^|dS| residuals. Hence K(S) <= 2^|dS| + 1. Consequence: min over orders of max over prefixes of K is at most 2^vs(F) + 1, where vs is the vertex separation number of the primal graph. Scope: conjunctive formulas with bounded factor size, any n. Not new: standard pathwidth-to-OBDD fact. Does not give a polynomial width for random 1-in-3 formulas, where vs is linear in n.

label: S0093
statement: statement: For a positive 1-in-3 CNF and a fixed variable cut with b clauses meeting both sides, the number of distinct residual Boolean functions is at most 4^b+1. For each crossing clause, assigning its variables on the processed side leaves one of at most four residual conditions on the unprocessed variables (including constant true/false). The conjunction of all clauses wholly on the processed side contributes only a global zero/nonzero flag; clauses wholly on the unprocessed side are common to every residual. Hence each residual is determined by a tuple of at most b crossing-clause forms and that flag, giving at most 4^b+1 possibilities.

label: S0094
statement: statement: For the positive 1-in-3 formula F(x0,x1,x2) defined by x0+x1+x2=1 with Boolean variables, every variable order has maximum number of distinct residual rows 3 and maximum rational cut-matrix rank 2. By symmetry it suffices to inspect prefix sizes k=0,1,2,3. At k=0 the single cut row is nonzero, so the width/rank are 1/1. At k=1, the two rows indexed by x0=0 and x0=1 are (0,1,1,0) and (1,0,0,1); they are distinct and linearly independent, giving 2/2. At k=2, rows indexed by (x0,x1)=00,01,10,11 are respectively (0,1),(1,0),(1,0),(0,0), giving 3 distinct rows and rank 2. At k=3 the rows are the one-column values of F, with both 0 and 1 occurring, giving 2 distinct rows and rank 1. Thus the maxima are 3 and 2; this repairs the incorrect claim that the k=1 cut has rank 1.

label: S0095
statement: statement: Let F be a conjunction of positive EXACT1 clauses, each on three distinct Boolean variables, and fix a variable cut with b crossing clauses. The number of distinct residual Boolean functions after assignments to the processed side is at most 3^b+1. For a crossing clause with one processed variable, the residual condition is one of x+y=1, x+y=0, or false; with two processed variables it is one of x=1, x=0, or false. Thus each crossing clause contributes at most three possible residual functions. label: S0096
statement: statement: Let F be a conjunction of positive EXACT1 clauses, each on three distinct Boolean variables, and fix a cut of the variables into processed set X and unprocessed set Y. If exactly b clauses meet both X and Y, then F has at most 3^b+1 distinct residual Boolean functions on Y as assignments to X vary. Proof: A clause wholly in X is either satisfied or violated by an assignment to X; all such clauses together contribute one global flag. If any is violated, the residual is the zero function. Clauses wholly in Y form a fixed common conjunct. For a crossing clause, let p be its number of variables in X (p is 1 or 2), let q=3-p, and let a be the number of its X-variables assigned 1. Its residual condition on its q Y-variables is that their sum equals 1-a. For p=1, a is 0 or 1, yielding respectively a two-variable EXACT1 condition or a two-variable zero-sum condition. For p=2, a is 0, 1, or 2, yielding respectively a unary value-1 condition, a unary value-0 condition, or the identically false condition. Thus each crossing clause has at most three possible residual functions. The tuple of these forms for the b crossing clauses, together with the global flag, determines the full residual after conjoining the fixed Y-only clauses. When the flag is true there are at most 3^b such tuples; when false all assignments yield the same zero residual. Therefore the total is at most 3^b+1. In particular, for any fixed variable order whose every prefix cut has at most B crossing clauses, its OBDD width at every level is at most 3^B+1. This is a boundary-based width bound; it makes no claim relating B to rational cut rank and does not settle G0001.

statement: Repair of S0094: For F(x0,x1,x2)=1 iff x0+x1+x2=1 on Boolean variables, every variable order has maximum residual-row count 3 and maximum rational cut-matrix rank 2. Proof: F is symmetric, so every order is equivalent under a variable permutation. For the cut after zero variables there is one nonzero row, hence count 1 and rank 1. After one variable, using remaining assignments 00,01,10,11 as columns, the rows for the processed bit 0 and 1 are respectively (0,1,1,0) and (1,0,0,0). They are distinct and linearly independent over Q, so count 2 and rank 2. After two variables, rows for processed assignments 00,01,10,11 over the final bit are (0,1),(1,0),(1,0),(0,0); hence there are 3 distinct rows and rank 2. After all variables the one-column rows are the attained values 0 and 1, giving count 2 and rank 1. Taking maxima gives 3 and 2. label: S0099
statement: statement: For every finite Boolean matrix M over Q of rank r, the number of distinct rows of M is at most 2^r. Proof: Let V be the rational row space of M, with dimension r. Choose r coordinate positions J such that coordinate projection V -> Q^J is injective, by taking pivot coordinates of a basis matrix of V. This projection is also injective on V intersect {0,1}^m. Its image lies in {0,1}^J, which has 2^r elements. Every distinct row of M belongs to that intersection, so there are at most 2^r distinct rows. If r=0, V={0}, and the conclusion still holds.

statement:
statement_start: For every positive EXACT1 CNF F whose clauses use three distinct Boolean variables, and every cut X|Y crossed by b clauses, the number of distinct residual Boolean functions on Y induced by assignments to X is at most 3^b+1.
proof: For an assignment to X, its residual is the conjunction of the fixed Y-only clauses, the residual conditions from crossing clauses, and a flag for whether all X-only clauses are satisfied. statement:
statement: For every positive EXACT1-3 CNF F and every partition of its variables into L and R, if b clauses intersect both sides, the number of distinct residual Boolean functions F|_x on R induced by assignments x to L is at most 2^b+1.
proof: For each assignment x to L, first test every clause wholly contained in L; if one fails, F|_x is the identically false function. For every crossing clause C, record t_C(x), the number of its variables in L assigned 1. If t_C(x)>=2, then the exact-one constraint cannot be satisfied for any assignment on R, so again F|_x is identically false. Otherwise every t_C lies in {0,1}. The value of F on an assignment y to R is the conjunction of all clauses wholly in R and, for each crossing clause C, the condition sum_{v in C intersect R} y_v = 1-t_C(x). Thus for two left assignments passing the checks with the same vector (t_C) over the b crossing clauses, their residual functions agree on every y. There are at most 2^b such vectors and at most one additional false residual, giving the bound.
scope: All finite positive exact-one 3-CNF formulas, arbitrary variable cuts; b is the number of clauses meeting both sides. This is a general proved-step candidate, not a P vs NP result.

label: S0106
statement: statement: Cut-factorization rank bound for tensor networks. Let G be a finite graph partitioned into vertex sets A and B. Each edge e has an index set [d_e], d_e positive, and each vertex carries an arbitrary rational tensor indexed by its incident edges and an optional finite external input x_v. Let F(x_A,x_B) be the scalar from summing the product of vertex tensors over all edge indices. If C is the set of edges crossing the partition and D=product_{e in C} d_e (empty product 1), then the rational rank of M[x_A,x_B]=F(x_A,x_B) is at most D. Proof: For each assignment z to the indices on C, contract all tensors and summed indices internal to A while fixing C to z, obtaining u_z(x_A); contract the B side analogously to obtain v_z(x_B). Regrouping the finite contraction by z gives F(x_A,x_B)=sum_z u_z(x_A)v_z(x_B). Thus M is a sum of D outer products, each of rank at most one, so rank_Q(M)<=D. This allows arbitrary rational entries, signs, cancellation, and finite external-input domains. It bounds a specified vertex cut only; it asserts nothing about optimal contraction orders, bit complexity, or the min-over-orders OBDD/rank gap.

statement:
statement: Let F be a conjunction of positive EXACT1 clauses, each on three distinct Boolean variables. For a fixed variable cut X|Y, let b1 and b2 be the numbers of crossing clauses with respectively one and two variables in X. The number of distinct residual Boolean functions on Y induced by assignments to X is at most 2^b1*3^b2+1. Proof: a crossing clause with p variables in X leaves the condition that its Y variables sum to 1-a, where a is the number of assigned 1s in X. For p=1 there are at most two possible residual forms; for p=2 there are at most three. The Y-only clauses are a common conjunct. All X-only clauses contribute a single global flag; if false the residual is zero, and otherwise the tuple of crossing forms determines it. Thus there are at most 2^b1*3^b2 tuples and one additional zero residual. Consequently, for any fixed variable order, the OBDD width at each cut is at most 2^b1*3^b2+1.
proof: For each assignment to X, every X-only clause is either true or false. If any is false, the entire residual is the zero function. Otherwise, each crossing EXACT1 clause reduces to the condition that the sum of its Y variables equals 1 minus the number a of its X variables assigned 1. When p=1, a∈{0,1}, hence at most two forms. When p=2, a∈{0,1,2}, hence at most three forms. The conjunction of all Y-only clauses is fixed. Therefore, among assignments for which the X-only flag is true, the residual is determined by a tuple with at most 2^b1*3^b2 possibilities; assignments with false flag contribute at most one additional residual, the zero function. The OBDD consequence follows because its width at a cut equals the number of distinct residual functions there.

label: S0116
statement:
statement: For any Boolean function f:X×Y→{0,1}, any fixed cut X|Y, and any field K, let M be its 0/1 communication matrix over K, let r=rank_K(M), and let D be the number of distinct rows of M. Then D≤2^r. Consequently, for every variable order π, the maximum number of residual functions at a cut is at most 2^{max_cut rank_K(M_cut)}; minimizing over π gives W_OBDD(f)≤2^{W_rank,K(f)}.
proof: Let U be the row space of M, of dimension r. The coordinate functionals on K^Y restrict to a spanning set of U*, so choose coordinates y_1,...,y_r whose restrictions form a basis of U*. The map φ:U→K^r given by these coordinates is injective. Every row of M is in U and has only 0/1 entries, so its image lies in {0,1}^r. Distinct rows therefore have distinct images, proving D≤2^r. If r=0, U={0} and D≤1. At a variable-order cut, rows correspond exactly to residual functions on the unprocessed variables. Apply the bound at each cut, then minimize over orders; monotonicity of 2^x gives the stated inequality.
scope: All finite Boolean functions, fixed variable cuts and variable orders, and any field K. This comparison does not construct a family attaining an exponential gap.

statement: statement_start: REPAIR of S0104: Let F be a positive EXACT1 3-CNF on n variables and m clauses with three distinct variables per clause. For a fixed variable order whose every prefix cut has at most B crossing clauses, exact #SAT is computable in O((n+m) * 3^B * poly(B)) arithmetic operations. Proof: Maintain a map from residual signatures to counts. A signature comprises (1) a failure flag, and (2) for each of the at most B crossing clauses, a residual condition from the set {EXACT1 on 3 vars, EXACT1 on 2 vars (sum=1), EXACT1 on 1 var (value=1), forced-0, forced-1, false}. There are at most 7^B * 2 signatures. Initialize with the empty assignment (flag=false, all clauses in future set) with count 1. At step k (variable v = order[k]), for each signature, branch on v=0 and v=1. To update: only clauses containing v change status. For each such clause, update its residual condition in O(1) time using a precomputed transition table (7 states x 2 values). Clauses not containing v keep their condition. After updating both children, merge identical signatures by summing counts. Merging uses hashing: O(7^B * poly(B)) per level. Total work per level: O(3^B * deg(v) * poly(B) + 7^B * poly(B)) = O(3^B * deg(v) * poly(B)) since 7^B = O(3^B * poly(B))? Wait, 7^B is larger than 3^B. Actually max signatures is 2 * 7^B. But the number of *active* signatures is at most 2 * 3^B + 1 because each crossing EXACT1 clause has at most 3 residual conditions when the failure flag is false (sum=0, sum=1, or false), plus the all-false state. So active signatures <= 2 * 3^B + 1. Updating a signature takes O(deg(v)) time (only clauses containing v change). Merging takes O(3^B * poly(B)) via hashing. Sum over n levels: O(3^B * poly(B) * sum_v deg(v) + n * 3^B * poly(B)) = O(3^B * poly(B) * (3m + n)) = O((n+m) * 3^B * poly(B)). At level n, sum counts of signatures with flag=false and no crossing clauses (all satisfied). This proves the runtime bound.

statement: statement_start: REPAIR of S0094: For the positive 1-in-3 formula F(x0,x1,x2) defined by x0+x1+x2=1 with Boolean variables, every variable order has maximum number of distinct residual rows 3 and maximum rational cut-matrix rank 2. Proof: By symmetry it suffices to inspect the order x0,x1,x2 and prefix sizes k=0,1,2,3. At k=0 the single cut row is the full truth table (nonzero), so width=1, rank=1. At k=1, rows indexed by x0=0 and x0=1 over (x1,x2) in order 00,01,10,11: F(0,x1,x2)=EXACT1(x1,x2) gives (0,1,1,0); F(1,x1,x2)=EXACT1(1,x1,x2) gives (1,0,0,0) since 1+x1+x2=1 requires x1=x2=0. These two rows are distinct and linearly independent (a(0,1,1,0)+b(1,0,0,0)=(b,a,a,0)=0 => a=b=0), so width=2, rank=2. At k=2, rows for (x0,x1)=00,01,10,11: 00->F(0,0,x2)=x2 gives (0,1); 01->F(0,1,x2)=1-x2 gives (1,0); 10->same as 01 gives (1,0); 11->impossible gives (0,0). Three distinct rows: (0,1),(1,0),(0,0), spanning 2D space, so width=3, rank=2. At k=3, rows are the values of F, both 0 and 1 occur, width=2, rank=1. Thus maxima over all cuts are 3 distinct rows and rank 2.
